modules.title: Our team and values
modules.body_md:
## Who we are

Window Works has been taking care of homes in the Triangle since 2007. It is
family owned, and the expertise behind it goes back a lot further than the
company does. That history is worth knowing because customers ask about it, and
because most of the rules in this training exist for a reason somebody learned
the hard way.

The company runs in four functions.

**Leadership** sets direction and owns the decisions that cross departments.

**Project management** hires and oversees the installation subcontractors, and
is the main contact for homeowners once a job moves into install.

**Admin** handles payroll, scheduling, and the paperwork behind every job.

**Sales** splits into B2B and B2C. B2B works with contractors, custom home
builders, and DIYers. B2C is homeowners and in-home sales, and we usually
install. People work one side or the other, not both.

Nobody expects you to have this straight in week one.

## These things are true at Window Works

**Customer service is everyone's job.** Not sales, not the installer, not the
PM. Every person is empowered to make sure the customer has a good experience.

**Each of us is a guide.** We exist to help customers find windows and doors
they will love. Whatever your role, your primary task is creating conversations
and tools that educate them so they make the right choice.

**Good judgment is valued and usually rewarded.** If a decision needs making
and nobody is around, use your best judgment.

**Fast is better than slow** unless there is a compelling reason to go slow.
That does not mean rushing into mistakes.

**Our time and energy are our most valuable assets.** This is why we hold
product minimums, service area limits, and other boundaries so firmly.

**We are preparing for growth,** which means stretching and changing. If you
are fearful or resistant to change, this is probably not the right job. Things
put in place one way may change in six or twelve months.

**Always be thinking about streamlining.** If you find a way to save time and
effort that also improves the customer experience, tell us. There is a good
chance it becomes how we do it.

**Never guarantee something you cannot personally deliver.** If a customer asks
for Jeff and he is out, do not promise he will call back today. Say you will
tell him they called as soon as he returns. This builds trust. Promising what
you cannot deliver breaks it.

**We do not do silos.** Teams share openly across functions.

**Do it, then report it.** If someone asks you to do something, do not say you
will work on it. Get it done and tell them it is done. Always close the
communication loop.

**Work each day as if it is your last,** meaning keep information accessible to
everyone. Subscriptions go to the company address, not your personal one. We
never use personal email for company business.

**Occasional overtime is normal. Consistent overtime is a planning or
communication failure** and we need to look at it.

**Own your mistakes.** Examine them, learn, tell people as soon as you notice,
then move on. Did you have a bad day, or a few bad minutes in an otherwise fine
day? The difference matters.

**More knowledge makes us more successful.** Every role here goes deep on
technical detail, whether tech stack or product. We cannot hold your hand
through all of it. Read, ask, watch, and seek out what you need to know.

modules.title: Employment contract and company policies
modules.body_md:
Third and last of the general HR videos. Your contract, the company policies,
the dress code, internal communication, vehicle use, and PTO.

## Your contract

Filled in per person: start date, position title, compensation. Covers benefits
you are entitled to, the 90 day probationary period with a review at the end,
our right to drug and alcohol testing, maintenance and return of company
property, and paid time off that does not apply during probation. Both sides
sign and you keep a copy.

## Conduct

Non-discriminatory workplace. Harassment or discrimination against coworkers,
customers, or anyone else based on protected characteristics is prohibited.
Report anything immediately to your supervisor, or above them if they are
involved. Investigated promptly and confidentially.

Divisive topics can be discussed respectfully, but not where it becomes
disruptive or creates a hostile environment. No offensive language or imagery
on clothing.

Vendors, drivers, subcontractors, and clients move through constantly. The
office is never as private as it feels.

Tell your supervisor about any accommodation you need, including medical
conditions we should be aware of.

## Hours and attendance

Store hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 5. Full time is 40 hours within
those. Roles that need different hours, like a PM meeting a crew early, can
adapt with reasonable discretion as long as they stay at 40. A permanent
alternate schedule needs written supervisor approval.

**In-home sales hours are more flexible.** You are on the clock when you are
working, you may take a 6:30 appointment or meet someone on a weekend, and you
are not expected in the office at 8:30.

**Overtime needs approval in advance.** We cannot pay it retroactively.

**Absence: phone or text your supervisor no later than 30 minutes before your
start time.** Check in each day you are out unexpectedly, unless your
supervisor already knows the situation and roughly how long you will be gone.

**Three consecutive no call no show days is voluntary job abandonment and
results in termination.**

Performance evaluation at 90 days, then annually.

## Equipment and appearance

Zero tolerance on working under the influence of drugs or alcohol.

Everyone keeps their own space clean and we collectively handle shared areas
and trash. Cleaners come weekly or biweekly, we cover the gaps.

You maintain the equipment assigned to you. Negligence or loss may be your
financial responsibility. Normal wear and tear is not.

Dress code applies to all customer-facing and office roles including sales,
admin, operations, and project management. Highlights: clean and wrinkle-free,
no holes or stains, logos smaller than a credit card, name tag at a
customer's house and when you are on assigned showroom coverage, not needed
otherwise in the office. Company or vendor branded tops
are fine. No hoods unless Window Works branded. Khaki, navy, black, or gray
bottoms, clean jeans acceptable, no cargo, no stretch or knit pants. Closed toe
professional shoes, no sandals or crocs. Natural hair colors. Only Window Works
or vendor branded hats. Tasteful jewelry, nothing that becomes a hazard when
you are handling product. Deviations allowed when you are doing physical work
like unloading, but keep it clean and safe.

## Technology and confidentiality

Company technology is for business use.

Do not disclose proprietary, financial, customer, or operational information
outside the company. What you see in a customer's home stays there.

Follow security protocols including password protection.

On personal social media you speak for yourself, but confidentiality and
anti-harassment still apply.

## Internal communication

**Pipedrive is the primary channel** for anything about a specific customer or
job. Email is next where Pipedrive does not fit.

**All business through your company email.** Never personal.

**Respond to email within four business hours.** If it is informational,
acknowledge it. If it asks for a short action, do it and say it is done. Do not
reply saying you will work on it. If it is a longer task, give your best
estimate and email again when it is finished.

Texting and calls are for genuine urgency, though some customers and
subcontractors prefer text and that is fine.

Out for a full day or more: set an out of office naming your backup.

## Personal vehicle and mileage

Reimbursed at the federal standard mileage rate, which covers fuel, insurance,
maintenance, and depreciation.
[Look up the current rate](https://www.irs.gov/tax-professionals/standard-mileage-rates). Nothing vehicle-related is reimbursed
on top of it.

**MileIQ is required.** Classify each trip as business or personal by the first
of the following month so it can be reimbursed.

Your daily commute is not reimbursable. Work to a jobsite, client, or errand
is. A temporary worksite like a coffee shop or library counts only if you are
actually conducting business there. Personal detours are not reimbursable.

NC minimum liability of 30/60/25 required, and a copy of your license on file
from day one. Your personal insurance is primary. The company does not cover
damage to your vehicle or your deductible. Parking and tolls between
appointments are reimbursable with receipts. Traffic violations are your responsibility.

## PTO

Biweekly pay, 26 periods a year. The full calendar and your next payday are
on the Resources tab in this portal.

Five sick days, ten vacation days, eleven paid holidays.

Sick leave covers you or a child, spouse, or parent who needs care.

Submit PTO requests to the admin professional, who submits their own to the
operations officer. **It is not approved until you receive written approval.**
If you have not heard back, follow up.

Vacation requests in writing at least 30 days ahead. Changes need a new request
and new approval. Requests around Thanksgiving, Christmas, or New Year go in by
October 1 so staffing can be planned.

No rollover. Up to five unused vacation days are paid out annually. Everything
is forfeited on resignation or termination.

First year: accrual begins after the 90 day probation, at 0.4167 sick days and
0.833 vacation days per full month worked. After the first year you get the
full annual allowance, reset January 1.

modules.title: Our installation story
modules.body_md:
The best window in the world fails if it is installed badly. That is the whole
argument, and it is the one thing a competitor cannot copy by matching a
product line.

You will lose deals on price. You should not lose them on price without the
customer understanding what they are giving up.

## The problem with our differentiator

Everything that separates our installation from a cheap one is **invisible once
the job is done.** Two windows can look identical on day one and be completely
different products. One will still be sealed in fifteen years and one will be
letting air and water into the wall.

That is exactly why the cheap version skimps on these things. Nobody sees them.

So your job is to make the invisible visible during the appointment, before
they compare numbers. Not after.

## The three things we do that most do not

### 1. We do not cap

Capping means wrapping aluminum coil over the existing exterior wood trim
rather than replacing it.

It is fast, it is cheap, and it looks fine on the day. It also traps whatever
was underneath. If there is rot, capping hides it and lets it keep going, out
of sight, against the wall of the house.

We replace the trim. PVC on the outside, which will not rot, sourced locally
so we are not paying manufacturer trim prices for a system that does not fit
brick openings anyway.

When a customer has a quote that includes capping, that is not a cheaper
version of our job. It is a different job.

**What that costs, in a real case.** A homeowner with an Andersen E-Series
window, aluminum clad, top of the line, called us because it was leaking. They
assumed the window was bad. We ran a water test, spraying at specific points on
and around the unit to isolate where the water was getting in.

The window was fine. Rot around the opening had never been repaired when the
previous window was replaced. Once the rot was fixed, the leak stopped.

That is the whole argument in one job. The best window available failed because
of what somebody skipped years earlier. Rot that gets covered instead of cut
out does not go away, and eventually the customer blames the window.

### 2. Correct expansion joints

An expansion joint is the space left around the window during installation, the
gap between the window frame and the home's siding. Both materials need room to
move.

**We recommend 5/16 inch on most projects.** Materials may change that, but
that is the number.

This matters more here than most places. Central North Carolina can swing 70
degrees in a few days, and with our humidity, everything moves: the brick or
siding, the window frame, the casing and moulding, and the caulk itself.

**Both directions are a failure.** Too small and the frame bows when it tries
to expand with nowhere to go, which is where sticking sashes and failed seals
come from. Too large and the caulk breaks down, because it is filling more
space than it can function across.

Most installers do one or the other. Getting it right is not a step, it is a
measurement.

Before any of that, the window has to be **plumb, level, and square.** Plumb
means the sides are perpendicular to a level sill. Level across both the sill
and the head. Square means every corner is 90 degrees and the unit is not
racked. Nearly every operational problem in a window traces back to one of
those three.

### 3. Real foam, silicone caulk, properly tooled

**Minimal-expansion polyurethane foam formulated for windows and doors,**
around the full perimeter. Standard expanding foam from a hardware store bows
the frame. It is not the same product and it does real damage.

**Silicone-based caulk.** The exterior caulk sold at big box stores does not
flex enough. It goes brittle and cracks, and then you have gaps, water, and
rot. Acrylic is cheap and readily available and it dries out. Silicone stays
elastic and moves with the window for years.

**Tooled properly over correct joint prep.** A good caulk job is not
noticeable. A bad one has globs in some places and thin, tearing beads in
others, and that inconsistency is where the water gets in.

Gaps left unfoamed are the most common thing found behind a bad install.

## The seven signs, and how to use them

This is the most useful thing you can do in the first ten minutes of an
appointment. Look at the windows they already have and tell them what you see.

1. **A window that will not open.** The sash cannot glide because the unit is
   not plumb, level, or square.
2. **A window that will not lock.** Lock and keeper are out of alignment. Same
   root cause.
3. **Rain, wind, dust, or bugs coming through a closed window.**
4. **Sashes that will not stay put.** Raise it and it creeps or drops.
5. **A sill that is not level.** Raise the sash slightly, or crank the casement
   partway, and look at the gap between sash and sill. That gap is called the
   reveal. It should be even across the whole span. If it is not, the unit is
   bowed, crowned, or angled.
6. **Poor caulking.** Globs and thin spots, or the wrong caulk entirely.
7. **No proper expansion joint,** or one that is far too large.

Doing this in front of a homeowner establishes more authority than anything you
can say about yourself. You are not claiming to be good. You are showing them
you can see things they cannot.

## The door version: the reveal

Same idea, and it takes seconds.

The door reveal is the gap between the door panel and the frame around it. On a
good install it is even the whole way around. Never perfect, but close.

Follow the gap from top to bottom. Tight or touching at the top and wider
toward the bottom means the reveal is off. Visible rubbing is the same signal.

An uneven reveal means the door will stick, rub, or fight you when it seals.
The homeowner may not have noticed yet, but it will show up.

**Be honest about the cause.** An uneven reveal is not automatically a bad
install. The other cause is the house moving, and around here that is common.
Cary has heavy clay soil and homes keep shifting for decades after they are
built. A door installed correctly forty years ago can be out of reveal today
through no fault of anyone.

Saying that out loud is more credible than blaming whoever came before you, and
it sets up the sale rather than undercutting it.

**Because the fix is a product feature.** Andersen 400 Series hinged patio
doors have adjustable hinges that let you raise, lower, or shift the panel.
Their gliding doors adjust with a Phillips head at the roller. So when you tell
a homeowner their door is out of reveal because the house moved, you can follow
it immediately with a door that can be brought back into alignment when it
happens again. That is a real reason to choose a better door, and it is
specific to this market.

## What else is in our labor

Flashing integration appropriate to the method. Interior and exterior trim.
Debris haul away. The materials are in the price: caulk, shims, molding inside
and out.

We source our own PVC trim, stool, and sill pans locally rather than buying the
manufacturer's, because ours are better suited and cost less.

## The warranty

**Two years on workmanship**, from the date of installation.

That covers our installation. Manufacturer defects, including glass seal
failure and hardware failure, run through the manufacturer's warranty. Voided
by negligence, acts of God, or modifications by anyone other than us, including
the homeowner.

Know the number. It is one of the four things the Value Match Guarantee
compares against, and a competitor offering one year does not qualify as
equivalent.

## Who actually does the work

Vetted subcontractor crews, managed directly by our project manager, who hires
them, oversees them, walks the jobs, and is the direct contact for much of the
installation work.

**One crew has been with us seventeen years.** That is not a small thing in
this trade, and it is worth saying out loud. Crews that stay are crews that are
treated well and paid properly, and that shows up in the work.

## How to use this at the table

Bring it up before the price conversation, not after. Once someone is comparing
two numbers it is too late to explain why they are not comparable.

Walk the three things out loud. Foam, sealant, and trim. Use the words. Most
homeowners have never heard anyone talk about installation at this level and it
lands.

If they have another quote, ask what it says about the foam and the sealant and
whether they are capping. It usually does not say, and the question is more
persuasive than any claim you could make.

If they genuinely want the cheaper build, offer to re-spec our quote down to
that scope so the choice is theirs and fully informed. Most decline once they
see it written out.

## Related reading

Send these. They make the argument for you and they are ours.

- Seven Telltale Signs of a Bad Window Installation
- A Simple Water Test Can Determine if Windows Were Improperly Installed
- What Is a Door Reveal? How to Tell If Your Door Was Installed Right
- Should You Cap Your Windows? What Homeowners Need to Know
- Are Windows Installed from the Inside or the Outside of a Home?

You drive a lot in this role. This is how you get paid for it.

## The rate

The federal standard mileage rate.
[Look up the current rate](https://www.irs.gov/tax-professionals/standard-mileage-rates). It covers fuel, insurance,
maintenance, and depreciation. There is no separate gas reimbursement, because
the rate already includes it.

## The deadline that costs you money

Every trip has to be classified business or personal in the MileIQ app **by the
first of the following month**. Miss it and that month does not get paid. Set a
recurring reminder for the last day of each month.

## What counts

Reimbursable: office to a jobsite, office to a client, an errand you were asked
to run, travel between appointments.

Not reimbursable: your daily commute from home to work and back. Personal
errands. A stop at your house on the way back from a client.

A coffee shop or library counts only if you are actually working there, meeting
a client, or meeting a subcontractor. Going to Starbucks on your break does
not.

## Parking and tolls

Reimbursable between appointments, logged as incidental expenses with receipts
attached. Traffic and parking violations are yours.

## Insurance

You need North Carolina liability coverage of at least 30/60/25, and a copy of
your license on file from day one. Your personal insurance is primary in an
accident. The company does not cover damage to your vehicle or your deductible.

modules.title: How you get paid
modules.body_md:
Worth reading in week one rather than week six. It changes how you work.

## The structure

**Base salary: $20,000 per year.**

That is deliberately low, because this is a commission role. The base is a
floor, not a living. Your income comes from what you sell.

**Your first four weeks are paid at the equivalent of $40,000 annually.**
Training pay, so you are not trying to learn the job and produce at the same
time. It ends when you go live in the field.

## Commission

| | Up to $2M | Over $2M |
|---|---|---|
| Company generated leads | 8% | 10% |
| Rep generated leads | 10% | 13% |

**That table is worth a second look.** A lead you source yourself pays two to three points
more than one we hand you. On a $30,000 job that is $600 more in your pocket
for the same appointment.

Over the course of a year that difference is not small. A rep who does $500,000
of self-sourced volume earns $10,000 more than a rep who does the same volume
off company leads.

We generate a steady flow of vetted leads and you will not run short. But the
structure is telling you something: the reps who do best here are the ones who
also build their own pipeline. Referrals, past customers, neighbors of jobs in
progress, contractors who like working with you.

**Example from the comp plan:** a rep at $2.5M total volume, with $500,000 of
that self-sourced, earns roughly $230,000 including base.

## What a discount actually costs you

Commission is on sale price. Not gross profit, not margin. So a discount
reduces your commission proportionally.

On a $30,000 sale at 8%, you earn $2,400. Discount it 10% to $27,000 and you
earn $2,160. That discount cost you $240.

It cost the company about $3,000 in gross profit.

So you carry roughly 8% of every discount and the company carries the rest.
That is worth understanding honestly. It means discounting will always feel
cheaper to you than it is, and it is why there is a hard wall at 20% that goes
to Rose and Justin.

The discount stack is there to help you close a deal you would otherwise lose.
It is not a tool for handling an objection. See the pricing module.

## What else you get

**Medical and dental** for you and your family.

**401(k)** with a company match.

**Mileage** at the federal standard rate, plus use of company vehicles when
available. Classify your trips in MileIQ by the first of the following month so
they are reimbursed.

**An iPad** with everything on it.

## When you get paid

**Commission pays on the deposit.**

That is faster than most places in this trade, where reps wait until a job is
installed and paid in full. Here, the 50% deposit gets collected at the
Measurement Confirmation appointment, and your commission follows from there.

So a deal you close in your first week can be earning that same week.

**Financed jobs pay you the same way, and this one is worth understanding.**

On a financed job the customer puts down nothing, and Window Works receives
nothing from Synchrony until the job is complete. Even so, you are paid as
though a 50% deposit came in at the same point you would be paid on a cash job.

The company carries that cash flow so you do not have to.

Two things follow. There is no reason to steer a customer toward cash to get
paid faster, so sell them whichever way suits them. It costs the company real money to do it this way, and it is done
because we would rather our people not be waiting on a lender to get paid for
work they already did.

## The ramp

Training pay covers your first four weeks and ends when you go live. After that
you are on base plus commission.

Because commission follows the deposit rather than completion, the gap is
shorter than you might expect. But it is not zero. There is still a stretch
between your first appointment and your first check, so plan for it.

modules.title: Andersen line overview
modules.body_md:
Andersen is our number one brand. This is the map of their lines and where each
one fits. Every other Andersen module assumes you know this.

## The series

**E-Series.** Architectural collection. Aluminum clad over a wood frame, so no
rot on the exterior. The most versatile line they make.

**A-Series.** Fiberglass clad, Fibrex framing, real fiberglass sashes. Built
for coastal and high wind load. Excellent, low volume in our market.

**Big doors.** Moving glass wall systems: bifold, lift and slide, multi-glide.
They need serious wall engineering, minimum 2x6, and will not work on 2x4. That
suits new construction, not replacement. We have sold them to restaurants and
homeowners.

**400 Series.** Vinyl clad except the Woodwright. Mid-price. The workhorse,
proven over many years.

**200 Series.** Also vinyl clad. Windows use nominal sizing that cannot be
customized, so mostly new construction. But the 200 Series sliding glass door
is a top seller and a great product.

**100 Series.** Fibrex composite, no wood at all. Newer, evolving, and we sell
a lot of it. The new 100 Series double hung should become one of our top
sellers over the next decade. Their gliding windows are already our go-to for
screened porch conversions.

**Andersen Aluminum.** Exists. We do not sell it.

**Renewal by Andersen.** All Fibrex, slightly upgraded profile over the 100
Series. One of our top competitors. We do not sell it, and you will be asked
about it.

## Why we sell them

Founded in 1903, still family and employee owned, not publicly traded. Great
customer service. Parts available for windows that have not been made since the
1960s.

Hans Andersen ran a family lumber company in Bayport, Minnesota, bought his
brothers out, and started making windows. Shipping assembled windows was hard,
so he sold frames knocked down for assembly on site and boxed the sashes
separately, then shipped nationally by rail. He also built it as a mass
production line. Henry Ford was the Andersen of windows.

They invented the vinyl window in the 1960s, decided it was not structurally
sound, and abandoned it. Today they make no all-vinyl window.

The strongest thing you can say: we have them in our own homes.

modules.title: Navigating the homeowner pipeline
modules.body_md:
Most of your work as a B2C salesperson happens in the homeowner pipeline. We
also run pipelines for professional accounts, installation and services, and
soliciting reviews at the end.

Each deal card is a customer. By default you see only the deals you own.

Pipedrive is built on the idea that sales success comes from managing stages
and activities. Stages are the customer's journey: initial contact, measure
scheduled, quote delivered, initial deposit, and on to final payment.
Activities are the things you do to move them along: calls, emails, the visit.

## Card shading

**White** means open and actively being worked.

**Red** means rotting. Each stage has a set amount of time we would expect
between touches. Past that with no interaction, the card turns red and you are
at risk of losing the deal.

**Green** means won, and it also gets a green won sticker.

## Activity icons

The small circle on the card, which is different from the card shading.

**Red** is an overdue activity. Something you scheduled did not get marked
done.

**Yellow** is no next activity scheduled. That is a problem, because we always
want to know what happens next.

**Green** is something due today. Your to-do list.

**Gray** is scheduled for a future date.

**When it's all gray, you're done for the day.** Every deal you own should show
only gray icons when you finish work. Red means you missed something. Yellow
means we do not know what happens next. Green means something today is not
done.

## Won deals disappearing

Pipedrive is designed for one-and-done sales, so by default a won deal vanishes
from view. That does not work for us. If your later stages look empty, or the
installation pipeline looks empty, go to filters and turn on the all deals
filter. It is company-set and already available to you.

modules.title: Essential customer information
modules.body_md:
What we capture about every person, and why each field breaks something
downstream if it is wrong.

## Name

First and last, spelled correctly, **capitalized correctly.**

Three systems read this field. Appointment reminders by text and email, email
automation tags, and the contract documents that pull from the deal. Get it
wrong and the customer sees it three times.

Always fine to ask someone to confirm the spelling.

## Phone and email

**Double check the email.** The email sync is defined by the address on the
person record. If it is wrong here, your emails to that customer will not
attach to the deal even when you sent them to the right address. Silent
failure, and the whole thread goes missing for whoever picks the deal up later.

## Address

Needed if we are visiting.

**The zip code quirk.** Pipedrive autocompletes the address but does not show
the zip. It knows it, it just does not display it. Add a comma after USA, type
2, and it fills in. Known bug, years old, unlikely to be fixed.

The install team plans routes by zip, and we pull this address for mailers, so
it matters.

## How they heard about us

Ask every time it is not already there.

The booking widget asks. A popup does not, and often gives you only a phone,
email, and first name, sometimes not even a last name. So on those you are
gathering the last name, the address, and the source on first contact.

It matters because referrals get thanked. If a family member sent them, we want
to know who, and there is a hundred dollar referral bonus in the quote for
exactly that.

widget. Mechanism is the same, the name is not.

modules.title: Moving deals between stages
modules.body_md:
The goal is that Pipedrive reflects, **in real time**, what is happening with
a customer.

Not at the end of the day. Not before the weekly meeting. As it happens.

## Why real time matters

Automations fire on stage changes. If the update is late, the automation is
late.

**Move a deal to Measure Scheduled and the customer immediately gets a welcome
email** thanking them for requesting a consultation, with a teaser of our
Ingage presentation to get them looking forward to the appointment.

Send that after the measure already happened and it looks careless.

**Move a deal to Initial Deposit and it triggers a run of activities** for
admin and project management: moving it to the installation pipeline,
scheduling the final measure, updating payment details, confirming paperwork.
None of that starts until the stage moves.

## Three ways to move a deal

Drag and drop the card in the pipeline view.

Inside the deal, use the compact pipeline strip and click the stage.

Or the same strip in the deal detail. Careful with the dropdown next to it,
that moves the deal to a different **pipeline**, not a different stage.

## The point

You are the one working the deal, but the rest of the team depends on this
being accurate. Move it when it moves.

modules.title: Effective activity management
modules.body_md:
Stages are where a customer is. Activities are what you do to move them along.
Your scheduled activities are your to do list.

## Setting one

Name it whatever you want, or use a predefined activity. Most of what you will
use sits at the start of the pipeline: calls, emails, tasks, the free in-home
sales consultation. Final measure is the project manager. Ordering, order
acknowledgments, and scheduling installations belong to other roles.

**Always capture the time, and for consultations capture the end time too.**
The calendar treats the duration as how long you are busy. Set a consultation
for 30 minutes when it runs 90 and someone can book over you through the
website.

You can assign an activity to somebody else. Useful when a customer walks into
the store and a rep needs to follow up.

## The rule

**Pipedrive should always show what has happened and what will happen next.**

That is the whole discipline. Everything below follows from it.

## Never mark something complete that did not happen

If a customer cancels, do not mark the appointment done and book another. Now
it looks like two consultations happened.

Delete or edit the activity, then **write a note recording what actually
occurred.** Scheduled for the 17th at 11:30, called on the 15th to cancel.

Then schedule what happens next. Call to reschedule.

## Never leave a completed call with no notes

A completed call with an empty note tells nobody anything. Did you reach them?
Leave a message? What did you talk about?

If a customer calls the store about that conversation, whoever answers has
nothing.

Minimal is fine. "Left voicemail, trying to reschedule measure" does the job.
If you had a real conversation, write more. "Interested in E-Series, planning
to come to the store to see color samples" tells the next person everything.

The people who need this are admin, project management, and the installers,
especially when you are on PTO or out on another measure.

## Your activities view

The calendar icon in the sidebar. Filter by overdue, due today, upcoming, sort
by due date, filter by activity type.

**Worth checking when you close out a deal.** Won and lost deals can leave
future activities behind, and they will keep showing up as overdue even though
the card is gone from your pipeline view.

modules.title: Internal messaging with @ mentions
modules.body_md:
Fastest way to ask a colleague something about a specific deal without an email
chain.

## How

In the deal's **note** section, type @ and it pulls up the team. Start typing a
name and it autocompletes. Write your message and save. They get a notification.

You can pin a note so it stays at the top, useful for something you are holding
until close.

## The trap

**@ mentions do not work inside an activity.**

You can type @ and a name in an activity's notes. It will not autocomplete and
**it will not notify them.** It looks like it worked. It did not.

Always use the deal notes.

## What you will get from Rose

At some point you will get an @ message asking what the next activity is on a
deal, usually because it is showing the yellow no next activity icon.

That is not a nudge, it is the standard. Every open deal should always have a
next activity scheduled. See the pipeline module.

modules.title: Winning and losing a deal
modules.body_md:
## Losing

Click Lost, or drag the card into the lost bucket. Either works.

You will be asked for a reason. The list is set by admin. If none of them fit
what actually happened, tell us and we will add one.

**The reasons, and what each actually means:**

**Window Works declines to proceed.** Rare, and a company side decision. Talk
to your manager first, there is usually more going on.

**Home on the market.** We do not work with real estate agents quoting homes
that are listed. Those are usually negotiating tools and rarely become deals.
We are happy to work with the homeowner once they own it.

**Outside our service area.** 30 mile radius from Cary. Sometimes people find
us from a blog post or a maps search.

**Under our minimums.** Three windows or one door. Try to convert them to a
larger project, and help them understand prices only go up. If they truly need
one window, we are not their company.

**Lead time.** Sometimes their timeline is not something we can meet. Often
this is education: an Andersen E-Series window takes longer to build than a
vinyl one, and that is production time, not our scheduling.

**Cost.** They bought windows, just cheaper somewhere else. **Different from
deciding not to proceed at all.** Ask enough questions to tell those apart.

**Lost to follow-up.** They ghosted us. Try to reignite it first.

**Seal failure.** We got out there and they do not actually need new windows.
We never sell somebody something they do not need.

**Outside of scope.** They want windows plus siding, or something we do not do.
Try to catch it before the visit, though a popup or online booking may not tell
you.

**Customer gathering info, not ready.** Just getting a sense of cost. Worth
explaining that today's quote is the least they will ever spend.

**Materials purchased elsewhere.** They wanted a Pella or a Marvin, which we do
not carry. **Different from cost.** It is about product, not price.

**Decided not to proceed.** Sometimes life happens. We had a customer ready to
sign who then had a house fire.

## A lost deal is not gone

The card turns red and drops out of your open view. **Reopen it any time and
everything is still there.** Nothing is lost.

So there is no harm in marking a deal lost once you have genuinely worked it.
If they call back in three months, click reopen.

## Winning

Mark it won, or drag it to the won bucket. The card turns green.

**Move it to Initial Deposit immediately.** That is what triggers the run of
activities for admin and project management.

**Update the collect payment activity with real detail before marking it
done.** Never just tick it complete.

What we need every time: whether it was an initial deposit or paid in full, the
method, the card's last four or the check number, **and the amount.** Amount is
always required. A check number with no amount is incomplete.

Financing: note it is financing with Synchrony, which plan, and the amount
financed.

Admin handles moving the deal to the installation pipeline and updating the
payment policy and installation quote details from Vendo.

modules.title: The insights dashboard
modules.body_md:
Pipedrive's built in reporting. Anything preloaded came from Pipedrive, not
from us, and you should feel free to delete it and build what is useful to you.

We are not going to mandate reports. We are going to expect you to use them.

## Building one

Graph icon in the sidebar. Create, then Report. It defaults to a deal
performance report, which is the most useful base.

The AI report builder is new and honestly not there yet. Build manually, it is
faster.

Filters tell the report what you want to know. Segment groups the results.
Measure switches between deal count and deal value. Chart type is up to you.

Below the chart is the underlying table. The gear icon controls which columns
show, and you can export to Excel.

**Nothing here changes any deal data.** You are only changing how you look at
what already exists. You cannot break anything.

## One report worth building

Deals with no next activity. The filters are fiddly, so here they are:

- Deal status **is not** Lost
- Pipeline **is not** Solicit Review, since that is the end pipeline for won
  deals and we do not expect a next activity there
- Number of activities to do **is** 0
- Stage **is not any of** the final stage of every pipeline

Or simpler, if you only work homeowners: pipeline **is** Homeowners, activities
to do **is** 0.

## Heads up

The Pipedrive exit quiz asks you to upload a screenshot showing at least two
reports you have built. Go build some.

modules.title: Booking measure appointments in Pipedrive
modules.body_md:
Primarily for whoever picks up the phone when someone calls the store.

This used to be two steps, booking in mail and then adding the activity. It is
one step now, all in Pipedrive. Doing it the old way is what caused duplicate

## The sequence

## Three things that are critical

**1. Activity type must be Free in-home sales consultation.** That is what
tells the back end to route it to the measure calendar. A call, a task, or
anything else will not get there.

**2. Name the activity with the customer's name and nothing else.** The
reminder system reads the activity title as the person's name. Name it
something about the appointment type and customers get texts opening with "Hi,
Mrs. Sales Consultation." Spelling and capitalization matter, because that is
what they see.

**3. Set both the activity assignee and the deal owner** to whoever is doing
the measure. If only one is set, they cannot see it.

## What fills in automatically

do not re-enter them.

modules.title: How our pricing works
modules.body_md:
## The multiplier

**Our base is 2.04 times cost.**

The 2.00 is the margin. The 0.04 covers credit card processing, which is why
B2C customers never see a separate card fee. It is already in the number.

B2B is different. Many contractors pay by check, so baking a card fee into
every price would overcharge them. B2B gets charged a card fee separately when
they use one.

In Reeb, select the homeowner pricing template and it applies. In Vinyl Design,
you enter the margin manually. Either way you are not doing the math yourself.

**We do not go below the margin.** Everything below is a discount off the
2.04, not a change to it.

## Tax

**Tax applies to products, not to labor.** Rate is 7.25% in Wake County.

That includes rot repair. If you see a change order adder marked as a taxable
service, that is an error being corrected.

Watch the Vinyl Design exception: their quoting software already includes tax,
so the package adder in Vendo must have taxable service **off**. Checking it
double-taxes the customer.

## The discount stack

Two tiers, and they work differently.

**Applied directly to the multiplier:**

- **Three day deal.** 5% if they commit within three days.
- **Cash discount.** 8% if they are paying cash rather than financing.
- **Referral bonus.** $100 flat if a friend or neighbor sent them.

**Applied through the margin alignment factor:**

If you want to show an additional discount, say for a customer who came in
through a popup offering 20% off, add the margin alignment factor first. It
raises the price 11.11%, and then you apply either the **10% or the 5%
authorized discount**. Not both.

Because the factor and the 10% roughly cancel, this is how you show a real
discount without going below the floor. It has to go in before you build the
quote, not after.

**Past 20% total, you hit a wall.** Vendo requires authorization and texts
Rose and Justin. That is not a formality. If you are asking, have a reason.

One thing to watch: on a low value deal, the flat $100 referral can be enough
to push the total past 20% and trigger approval when nothing else would.

## Financing

Three options through Synchrony Bank:

- 18 months no interest, with interest billed during the promotional period and
  waived if paid in full before the term expires
- 10.99% APR until paid in full
- 5.99% APR until paid in full

Preapproval is required before an order is placed. **Financed orders collect no
deposit.**

Present these in the Price Kit. Enter the project total and it shows monthly
figures alongside the cash option.

## Deposit and payment

Cash, check, or card: **50% deposit**. Typically the Project Manager collects
it at the Measurement Confirmation appointment, but you can take it at the
table if the customer wants to pay then. Either way, log it in the collect
payment activity in Pipedrive with the method, the last four or check number,
and the amount. Amount is always required.

The balance is due when the project is complete.

Financing: no deposit.

We do not accept checks or cash by mail. Card is Visa, Mastercard, Discover, or
American Express.

**All sales are final.** No returns, refunds, or exchanges. Say this plainly
rather than letting a customer discover it later.

**A project counts as complete once all windows and doors are installed,** even
if screens have not arrived or a damaged sash is being replaced. Payment is due
then. Customers sometimes want to hold back money over a missing screen, so set
that expectation during the appointment rather than arguing about it at the
end.

## What the customer already knows

Our website publishes what an average customer spends. Many arrive having read
it. Know the number so you are not contradicting your own marketing.

Our minimum is **three windows or one door** per visit. Service area is a
30-mile radius from Cary.

## What is not in the price

Rot repair. It is excluded from every quote. If rot is found, the PM assesses
and a signed change order is required before repairs proceed.

Painting is optional and priced separately. Standard service means primed trim
only, with visible nail holes, and the customer does the sanding, filling, and
top coat. Painting service means we do it. It must be discussed during the
quote because they sign off on it in the installation agreement. If neither box
is checked, standard applies.

A Porta-John if the customer will not provide restroom access, roughly $350 per
week at their expense.

## When they say it is too much

This is the part that matters.

**Do not open with a discount.** The stack exists so you have room to close,
not so you have an answer to an objection. A rep who leads with price is
teaching customers to negotiate.

Go here first:

**Ask what their other quote actually says** about the foam, the sealant, and
whether they are capping. Most do not say. See the installation story module.

**Explain the Value Match Guarantee.** Say the whole phrase. Never "price
match," because we match what they get, not just what they pay.

**Offer to re-spec down** to the cheaper scope so the choice is theirs and
informed. Most decline once they see what comes out.

**Then, if you need it,** the three day deal gives them a real reason to decide
today rather than a reason to shop.

modules.title: The lineup, and what to lead with
modules.body_md:
You do not choose a brand. You look at what is in the house, decide the install
type, and the product follows.

This is why the needs assessment and the install type come first. Get those
right and this guide answers the rest.

**One rule before anything else: do not quote two or three different window
lines.** It creates confusion, the customer freezes, and then someone else
walks in with one window and one price and wins. Pick the right line and lead
with it.

## A. Existing old wood windows

**Full frame, standard** → Andersen 400 Series Tilt Wash

**Full frame, colonial home or they want a fiberglass composite exterior** →
Andersen 400 Series Woodwright, as the upgrade

Both use traditional wood window sizes, so no custom sizing. They share sizes
and many specs, so moving a customer between them is easy.

400 Series picture windows can be quoted to match, but note they are custom
sized. Picture windows do not follow traditional wood sizes even though the
double hungs do.

**Full frame casement** → Andersen 100 Series or 400 Series
- 100 Series if they want fully fiberglass composite, and it costs less
- 400 Series if they want a wood interior

Either way, casements get custom sized. That is true whether you are replacing
a double hung or an existing casement.

**Insert or replacement** → Andersen 100 Series double hung, casement, picture,
or gliding

**This is the preferred option and a much better solution than vinyl.** Lead
with it.

**Insert or replacement, vinyl option** → Vinyl Design Mountainview 1000, in
double hung, casement, picture, or gliding

## B. Existing vinyl windows

Remember this is always full frame vinyl. There is no wood frame to insert
into.

**Full frame** → Andersen 100 Series
**Full frame, vinyl option** → Vinyl Design

**Two things to check every time on a vinyl-to-vinyl job:**

**J-channel.** Verify the siding type and whether the new windows need one.
Vinyl windows offer J-channel as an integral, optional part of the frame.
Andersen does not, so it has to be sourced locally as additional material.

**Interior trim.** Do the existing windows use extension jambs or drywall
returns, and what depth? That determines whether you need interior cutbacks,
stops, or both.

## C. Entry and hinged doors

**Hinged patio doors** → Andersen E-Series, aluminum clad, or A-Series,
fiberglass

Unless you are specifically selling an all-fiberglass option, lead with these.
Both offer standard and custom sizes, traditional and contemporary styles, and
sizes you cannot get in other lines or brands.

**Hinged entry doors,** including front doors, single entry, and fire-rated →
ProVia, any series

Fiberglass is always preferable, but their steel doors are well made.

Andersen does make an entry door. Do not bring it up. The options are extremely
limited and you will sell a fiberglass door almost every time. We have sold
maybe eight to ten in fifteen years.

## D. Gliding doors

**Two panel:**

| Line | Material | Style | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 Series | Fiberglass composite | Contemporary | Most competitive |
| 400 Series | Vinyl clad | Traditional panels | Moderate |
| 200 Series | Vinyl clad | Contemporary, a few more options | Moderate |
| A-Series / E-Series | Fiberglass / aluminum clad | Both, highly customizable | Higher |

**Four panel:** same as above, minus the 100 Series. It only comes as a two
panel.

## E. Specialty doors

**Moving glass wall systems,** outswing bifold, multi-glide, lift and slide →
Andersen Big Doors

**Roughly $1,700 to $2,300 per linear foot for the door alone,** before labor
or any wall work. A 16 foot opening is tens of thousands of dollars. Knowing
that lets you find out quickly whether it is a real conversation.

Custom only, minimum 2x6 wall, and a one to two week quoting process involving
an engineer and a site visit. Recognize one, set the expectation, and hand it
off. If you are quoting a whole house, break the big door out into a second
package so it does not hold up the rest.

**The economical alternative:** if they want that wide open feel, the 200
Series, 400 Series, or E-Series four panel gliding doors customize to around 16
feet and cost far less. We never use the word cheap. More economical, less
expensive.

## F. Specialty windows

**Architectural shapes,** half circles, trapezoids, rectangles, arches,
springlines → Andersen ASW

Almost always full frame. Always custom sized, regardless of brand or series.

modules.title: Using Vendo: navigation, adders, and final documents
modules.body_md:
The appointment flow, and everything from adders through to the customer
signing. Building Andersen windows in detail is the next module.

This and PR-021 together are the most important content in the library.

## Starting the appointment

An appointment may be waiting for you from Pipedrive. That automation is still
being worked out, so if it is not there, create it. Plus sign, lower right.

Existing customer, search and select. New, add them. **Capitalize the names.**
They pull into documentation if this becomes a win.

Additional contact adds a spouse or a contractor who needs to be on the
paperwork.

Vendo pulls in the property value, year built, and house size once you enter
the address.

**Do not hit Start until you know you will be quoting them that day.** Once a
deal starts you have to result it as won, lost, or pending. If nobody is home
or they cancel at the door, do not start it.

## Needs assessment

Eleven questions. **These are ours, not Vendo's defaults.** Order does not
matter, and if you get the answers through normal conversation that is better.
It is an internal document to make sure you covered the bases.

Windows, doors, or both. Previous replacement experience. Reasons for
considering. Age of the existing units. Energy efficiency goals. Style change.
UV protection for furniture and flooring. Project timing. HOA guidelines.
Installation questions.

**The most important one is whether they have ever had window or door
replacement done before.** Most people have not. They have put it off for
years, and there is usually real sticker shock and no familiarity with the
terms, including something as basic as full frame versus pocket insert.

You are gauging where they sit on a scale of one to ten and then meeting them
there.

Also worth setting early: this is a construction project. There will be dust
and debris. We clean it up, but people who do not expect it get upset on day
one.

## The rule about quoting one line

**Do not quote two or three different window lines.**

It creates confusion, they freeze, and then somebody else walks in with one
window and one price and closes them.

And we want them getting the right product. We do not walk in and tell people
what they are getting, that is not our process. We ask, they participate, and
then we guide.

## The flow

Inspection and Configure are nearly the same thing. Inspection's Save only
takes notes forward, which is a waste of time.

**Use Configure Now and build each window as you measure it.** Room by room.
Do not collect all the measurements and then sit down to quote, it takes far
longer and you end up camped in someone's house.

Hand the homeowner your iPad while you measure. Keep talking. Silence costs you
the relationship, and the connection is what closes the deal later.

## Demo

Three tiles. **Open the blue Ingage one** to present. The black one with the
suitcase is only there so Vendo can email them a link at the end. The third is
Price Kit, and you come back to it after the quote to show financing.

Load the presentation before the appointment so it opens fast.

## Configure

Build the windows and doors. Andersen is directly integrated because Vendo is a
Paradigm product and Paradigm built Andersen Access. Reeb and ProVia import by
quote number. Vinyl Design does not integrate and needs the workaround.

Building Andersen windows in detail is its own module, PR-021.

**Adders.** Line level sits inside each Andersen line item. Project level sits
at the end. Margin alignment factor goes in first. See the adder traps sheet,
this is where quotes go wrong.
## Quote and price kit

Take the project total into the Price Kit under Demo and enter it as the
project total. That shows them the cash number alongside the three Synchrony
financing options with monthly figures.

Three dots, upper right, applies discounts. See the pricing module. Over 20
percent triggers an approval text to Rose and Justin.

Bring the discounts back into Vendo on the quote screen.

## Documents

Proceed. Two documents are required and pre-selected, so you cannot deselect
them.

**Installation agreement.** Estimate the duration in days. Describe the units
in plain words. Moulding application, casings, back band, exterior casing, and
quantities for sill nosing replacement, storm window removal, and affixing
window treatments.

Talk them through it rather than letting them read it cold. The things that
cause problems later are all in here:

- Rot repair is not included. If we find it, the PM assesses and a signed
  change order is required before repairs proceed.
- We do not reinstall or calibrate security systems, or program smart locks and
  keypads.
- We do not guarantee existing blinds, curtains, shutters, or shades will fit
  the new windows. They can come to the showroom and check.
- We do not reuse existing mouldings or casings. They are usually brittle and
  removing them intact is not worth the carpentry.
- If they bought their own door hardware, it has to be compatible and ready on
  install day. We cannot fit a dummy handle, the strike plate will not line up,
  and the door cannot be secured.
- Painting: standard service means primed trim, visible nail holes, and they do
  the sanding and painting. Painting service means we do it, and it has to have
  been in the quote as an adder.
- Restroom access. Comes up maybe once a decade, but if they will not designate
  one we coordinate a Porta-John at roughly 350 dollars a week at their expense.
- Final walkthrough within 48 hours of completion.
- Labor warranty is two years on workmanship. Manufacturer defects, including
  seal failure and hardware, go through the manufacturer.

**Payment policy.** Nothing for you to fill in, but talk through the middle
section. A project counts as complete once all windows and doors are installed,
even if a screen has not arrived or a damaged sash is being replaced. Payment
is due then. Set that expectation now rather than arguing about it later.

## Signing

Ask how they want to sign. **On this device right now** is the one call close
and what you want. Personal device means they want to think about it or talk to
a spouse who is not there.

Hand them the iPad. They review, agree to the electronic signature consent, and
initial and sign. Drawn or typed, both fine.

If they refuse electronic signature consent the deal stalls, because we would
need to print everything. It almost never happens.

They hand it back, you hit proceed.

## Sending

Both signed contracts go automatically. You can add the inspection report,
useful if there was a lot of damage, and the emailed Ingage presentation if
they asked for it.

CompanyCam is the better route for photos. Vendo caps at around ten.

Finish sends the customer an email with their documents, and sends admin,
operations, and the project manager everything they need to start scheduling
the final measure and ordering.

## If they do not sign

Result the deal as pending or lost. Do not leave it open.

modules.title: Quoting Andersen windows in Vendo
modules.body_md:
Building the product. PR-020 covers the appointment flow and the close.

Vendo is a Paradigm product and Paradigm also built the Andersen Access quoting
software, which is why Andersen is directly integrated and ProVia and
Therma-Tru are not.

## Inspection versus Configure

They are nearly the same thing.

Inspection's **Save** only carries your notes forward. It does not quote
anything. That is a waste of time.

**Use Configure Now and build each window as you measure it,** room by room. Do
not collect all the measurements and then sit down to quote. It takes far
longer and you end up camped in someone's house.

Put the iPad down while you measure. Some reps hand it to the homeowner. Keep
talking either way, because silence costs you the relationship.

One quirk: if you pick double hung in the inspection notes, Configure will only
offer you double hungs. Coming in through Configure directly gives you
everything.

## What not to quote

The product list includes things we do not sell. **Garden windows and hopper
windows, ignore them.**

In the double hung list specifically:

- **200 Series Tilt Wash** is new construction only. Off the table for
  replacement.
- **E-Series sash replacement kit,** and sash kits generally, never.
- **Narrowline to Tilt Wash conversion kit,** skip 98 to 99 percent of the
  time.
- **StormWatch and coastal DP50 or impact** are for genuinely coastal work.
  Double the price and double the weight.

## Building a window

Installation method: nailing flange for new construction.

Sizing shows you the unit dimension and the rough opening alongside the sash
size. The unit is bigger than the sash by roughly three quarters of an inch for
the frame, and the RO is bigger again for shims and insulation.

Equal sash, cottage, or reverse cottage. You can see which a house has from
outside.

Colors, jamb liner colour (grey by default if the window is black), glass.
**Low-E4 SmartSun is our default for this market.** Standard Low-E4 is already
efficient out of the box. HeatLock works well but is designed for northern
climates.

Tempered where code requires it. See the tempered glass reference sheet.

Grilles: full divided light, simulated divided light, removable interior, or
Finelight which is Andersen's between the glass. Match what the customer has,
including the bar width, and get as close as Andersen offers. There is no
industry standard and no custom widths.

If the default pattern is not what they have, use specified equal light and
enter the custom pattern. Two wide by two high gives you a four over four.

Sash lifts: none on the Tilt Wash. Hardware traditional unless they want
estate.

**Full screen, always.** Andersen charges the same for a half screen as a full
one. TruScene is a real upsell and customers love it.

Extension jambs if it is not a 2x4 wall. Andersen full frame windows are
4-9/16 and reach the interior on a 2x4. 6-9/16 for a 2x6, 5-1/4 for old plaster
walls.

**Stool: none.** We source our own locally.

## The advanced tab

**We are in the South-Central ENERGY STAR climate zone.** See the correction
note below.

Sizing method: Unicode standard for most old wood double hungs, custom only if
you need it.

Specialty glass, mostly bathroom privacy, and each option prices differently
because it is based on glass area.

High altitude: no. We are a couple of hundred feet.

Gas filled goes to argon automatically. Simulated check rail: no.

Grille colours, exterior and interior, two tone if the window is.

DP upgrade: no, that is coastal.

**Window opening control devices.** Code triggers when a window is 18 inches or
less from the floor with more than a 60 inch drop outside. Screwed in, factory
or field applied. Most people do not want them, but offer them to a family with
small children.

Exterior trim: no. We use PVC, and Andersen's does not work in brick.

Room location, then save.

## Saving time

**Copy** creates a new opening with the same configuration. Rooms repeat,
especially upstairs, so this saves real time. Update the quantity if there are
two identical units in one room.

Copying within Configure asks whether to bring your previous choices across.
Say yes, and it carries glass, colour, hardware, and screens.

**Copy does not bring the adders.** Every copied unit needs its adders added
separately. This is the easiest thing in Vendo to miss, because the copy looks
finished. Missing them means we install a window for free, and there is real
labor and material in that.

We are here to give a fair price and a good product, not to give it away.

## Mulling

Copy and mull, or mull new unit, then pick the location: top, sides, bottom.

Mulling location means where it gets assembled. **Andersen at the factory** for
most things. Field for very large or unusual configurations, which our crews
can handle.

Mull material: one eighth non-reinforced is fine for a typical twin. 3/16 steel
for heavier work.

**V-notch: always no.**

Half circles and other complementary shapes mull on top. Grille patterns on
half circles are fiddly and there are a lot of options.

Trimstop on the inside: yes. Grille alignment: usually yes on transoms and half
circles, no when the geometry does not allow it. Drip cap: yes, flexible white.
**Arch casing: none.** We use flex molding bought locally.

## Where the adders go

Inside the window itself. Configure, Edit, then the Adders tab. Not at project
level, because Andersen is directly integrated.

Full detail is in PR-030 and the adder traps reference sheet.
modules.author_note:
**Correction, and this video is being refilmed.** It states we are in the
North-Central ENERGY STAR zone. **Wake County is South-Central,** confirmed on
the ENERGY STAR site in August 2026. The video also tells reps to hold the line
if a customer questions it, which makes the error worse.

South-Central criteria: U-Factor 0.28 or lower, SHGC 0.23 or lower. The Most
Efficient tier at U 0.20 or lower is what qualifies for federal tax credits.

modules.title: Quoting Andersen doors in Vendo
modules.body_md:
Configure, then the **Patio Doors** tab rather than Windows, then the plus
sign.

The list is long and looks repetitive because it is. Hinged and sliding, with
sidelight and transom options, across every Andersen series.

**Faster way to find something:** use the product type filter. Choose gliding
patio door and it narrows immediately. Scrolling for a door while a customer
watches is not a good look.

## The height rule, and it is the one that costs money

Andersen offers 6'8", 6'11", and 8'0".

**If you are replacing an existing standard door, choose 6'11".** Unit size is
82-3/8, rough opening 83.

Their 6'8" is undersized and will not fit.

Here is the part that confuses people. On a Therma-Tru or ProVia you would
choose **their** 6'8", because for them that is the bigger size. Those
manufacturers size by panel plus frame. Andersen sizes the entire unit. Same
words, different meaning.

## Traditional versus contemporary

Traditional, also called French wood, has wider framing around the glass.
Contemporary has less framing and a cleaner look.

More people are choosing contemporary on hinged doors lately, but traditional
is still a real option. Same quality either way. Walk the customer through it.

## Configuration, viewed from the exterior

**Active left passive right,** or the reverse, or configurations where one
panel is fixed, or both are fixed.

The **active** door is the everyday door and opens first. The **passive** door
opens second and only after the active one is open.

## Colors and wood species

You can split the color, black outside and white inside for example.

Interior is pine, oak, maple, cherry, or mahogany.

**Never choose a high-end wood species and then paint over it.** There is no
point putting white paint on mahogany. Andersen sometimes allows the
combination and sometimes removes it. If it is available, do not take it.
Species upgrades are for staining or leaving unfinished. If it is getting
painted, choose pine.

## Glass

Dual pane, Low-E SmartSun as our default.

**All door glass is tempered by federal law.** Andersen, Marvin, Pella,
Therma-Tru, Plastpro, ProVia, all of them, regardless of how much glass is in
the door. There is no decision to make.

**STC glass is sound control,** and it is worth offering. Sound abatement glass
for a customer on a busy road, backing onto a highway, or in a downtown condo.
It is an upcharge and it makes a real difference.

Reveal spacers default to stainless steel, with black and white available.

Grilles are increasingly rare on doors. Most people want the view.

## Hardware, and this is a hard boundary

Every style is a different price. FSB and Ashley Norton are upcharges,
especially on a double door where there is a handle set on each side. Even the
standard Andersen options are not cheap.

**You must use Andersen hardware.** The multi-point lock is built into the
door.

If a customer does not like any of the options, the answer is no, and **we
cannot point them anywhere else.** This is what Andersen recommends and it is
what we sell.

If they go and buy hardware somewhere else, **we will not install it.** It is
not part of the installation and we take no responsibility for how the door
then operates. They are welcome to do it, on their own.

That is a genuine boundary, not a soft one. Either they choose from what
Andersen offers, or they get a door with no hardware installed.

**Split finish** lets you run different styles or colors inside and out, which
pairs well with a split colour door.

**Finishes are specific to each hardware style, not a universal palette.**
Anvers, for example, only comes in satin nickel, oil rubbed bronze, and bright
brass. If a customer insists on bright brass, you have to work out which sets
offer it.

## Key locks are not included

**They are always an add-on with Andersen. Never a default.**

**Ask every single time.** We have had customers assume a key lock was included,
find out it was not, and we ended up ordering it after the fact, which costs us
because nobody asked.

They can run over a hundred dollars.

If they want it keyed to match the rest of the house, that is a locksmith. We
do not do that.

## Screens

Unlike windows, doors do not default to a screen.

Andersen's hinged door screen is a double hinged arrangement and it is odd.
**Probably do not offer it.** If a customer wants a screen on a hinged door, a
phantom screen is the better answer.

## The advanced tab

PG upgrade: no in this market.

Unit code `FWHID` is French wood hinged in-swing door, and 60611 is the size.
The swing is baked into the product you select, unlike Reeb where the software
asks you during the quote.

**Frame depth: 4-9/16 for a 2x4, 6-9/16 for a 2x6. This cannot be changed
later.** Get it wrong and we are ordering a new door, or at minimum a new
frame, with all the cost and labor that carries. Check the wall depth. This
applies to windows too.

Sill: gray or bronze appearance. **Andersen does not offer a mill or aluminum
finish sill.**

Remodel sill bracket: no. Our crews supply whatever support the door needs.

Glass stop profile: chamfer is the automatic default on a traditional door,
ovolo is the alternative.

Threshold: none. Oak and maple are available, they are expensive, and we supply
them in the field.

Specialty glass: usually none. Privacy glass on a back patio door is rare,
front doors are a different conversation.

High altitude: none.

**Hinged doors are always factory assembled.** No option. Every Andersen hinged
door arrives pre-hung in the frame. Gliding doors are a different story, below.

Then hardware styles come back for the split finish, along with hinge colour,
panel stop finish, temporary construction hardware (no, the doors ship with an
allen key that locks them), corrosion resistant locking mechanism (coastal
only), and exterior trim (none, we supply our own).

## Gliding doors: always unassembled

**With the exception of the 100 Series, which has no option, every Andersen
two panel patio door can be ordered factory assembled or unassembled. Always
choose unassembled.**

Four reasons:

It is **$100 to $200 less expensive**, which makes us more competitive.

Each panel and the frame are wrapped separately, so **one person can move and
deliver it** and it is far less prone to damage. Assembled, even a five or six
foot door is heavy and awkward.

It is **pre-drilled**. Our crews assemble the frame in 15 to 20 minutes with
the supplied screws and silicone.

And it is **easier to install**, because they can lift the frame into the
opening and build the door on site rather than wrestling a finished unit.

## The auxiliary foot lock is not optional

It defaults to none. **You choose one anyway, every time.**

Every Andersen sliding door we sell gets a foot lock. It acts as a deadbolt,
sitting at the bottom of the operating panel and locking into the frame. The
cost is minimal, and customers who did not know they wanted one want it as soon
as you show it to them.

We do not present it as an option. Match the finish to the interior colour.

## The 200 Series Narrowline

Worth knowing specifically, because **we sell more of this gliding door than
anything else.** Contemporary profile, available as one, two, or four panel.

Aluminum or gray appearance. **No bronze on this door.**

## Four panel gliders

Two middle panels open into a wide opening, the two ends are fixed. A genuinely
economical alternative to a bifold or multi-glide.

**Stock sizes run 10 feet to 16 feet,** which is 117 to 189 inches. It
customizes in eighth inch increments for odd openings, **but check the stock
sizes first because they are considerably less money.** You cannot go below 117
or above 189.

8 foot heights are popular here.

**Two foot locks on a four panel,** because there are two operating panels. On
this door they are close to essential: without them, operating one panel makes
the other move, and most people want one locked in place as the everyday door.

**Four panel doors only come unassembled.** There is no choice. Assembled you
would need a crane.

## Adders

Do not forget them. Patio door adders live inside the line item like windows.

Double door, single with two sidelights, four panel glider, whichever matches.

Add painting if the customer wants the trim painted. On a four panel, the
painting adder is the double door line at **quantity 2.**

quiz.q: You are replacing an existing standard exterior door with an Andersen hinged patio door. Which height?
A customer wants a mahogany interior and asks you to paint it white. What do you do?
options: Quote it, it is their choice
Do not. Painting over a high-end species is money wasted. If it is getting painted, quote pine.
Quote it but note it on the order

quiz.q: A customer does not like any of the Andersen hardware options and wants to buy their own. What do you tell them?
options: We can install anything they supply
We can recommend a few other suppliers
They must choose from Andersen. If they source their own, we will not install it and we take no responsibility for how the door operates.
We can order it through Andersen as a special item

quiz.q: A customer asks whether their new patio door comes with a key lock.
options: Yes, it is standard on Andersen doors
No. It is always an add-on with Andersen, so ask every time.
Only if they choose a multi-point lock

quiz.q: You quoted a 4-9/16 frame depth and the wall turns out to be a 2x6.
options: New door, or at minimum a new frame. It cannot be changed later.

quiz.q: How do you order an Andersen two panel gliding patio door?
options: Factory assembled, so the crew does not have to build it
Unassembled, always, except the 100 Series which has no option
Assembled on stock sizes, unassembled on custom

quiz.q: The auxiliary foot lock field defaults to none. What do you do?
options: Ask the customer whether they want one
Choose one. Every Andersen sliding door we sell gets a foot lock.
Only add it on four panel doors

quiz.q: A customer lives backing onto a busy highway and mentions road noise. What can you offer?
options: STC sound control glass, an Andersen upcharge that makes a real difference
Nothing, glass does not affect sound

quiz.q: A customer needs a 13 foot four panel glider. What do you check before quoting custom?
options: Nothing, four panel doors are always custom
Whether a stock size fits. Stock runs 117 to 189 inches and is considerably less money.
Whether the wall can carry it
Whether Andersen makes it in that width

modules.title: Understanding project adders in Vendo
modules.body_md:
Adders do two jobs. They configure pricing, and they capture the labor for
installation.

Getting them right is how we charge fairly. We do not want to overcharge, and
we absolutely do not want to give labor away.

**The adder traps reference sheet is the short version of this.** Read that
first, then watch this for the walkthrough.

## Margin alignment factor, first

Configure, Project Adders, Select Existing, Service Fees tab, check it, done.

Before you quote anything. It adds 11.11 percent so you have room to discount
back during the price conversation, with safeguards that should stop you going
below the floor.

## Where adders live

**Andersen windows and Andersen patio doors:** inside each line item. Build the
window, then the Adders tab.

**Therma-Tru through Reeb, ProVia, Vinyl Design, DSA:** project level, at the
end.

## Carpentry adders

The things the crew charges us for, so we charge for them.

Taking blinds down and rehanging them. Interior shutters, usually plantation,
which cost more than exterior because they are more work. Exterior shutters,
usually plastic and easier. Brickmold and sill nose replacement. Cutting
windows out of an opening, which comes up with bricked over openings, nailing
flanges, and old aluminum, and is far more labor than it sounds. Field cutting
and applying extension jambs. Siding repair and rot. Storm window removal,
rarer now but it still happens.

## Install type drives the price

Replacement, full frame, or new construction. Completely different labor and
material. See the install types reference sheet.

The one to watch: a screened porch conversion looks like new construction
because the opening is ready, but we are doing trim work, so it is full frame.

New construction is significantly cheaper and should only be selected when it
genuinely applies. In-home sales rarely sees it. The professional side does.

## United Inches

Width plus height. Tiers at 102 or less, 103 to 125, over 125. Bigger and
heavier means more to the subcontractors.

## Doors

Andersen patio doors work like the windows, adders inside the line item.

**Non-Andersen doors** is the tab for ProVia, Therma-Tru, and DSA. Door with a
transom, single, double, triple, single with two sidelights. **A transom is a
separate standalone price.** Miss it and the transom labor is unbilled.

**Big doors cannot be quoted in the field at all.** Too much involved, all
custom. Special quote, and you probably cannot give a price on site.

## Vinyl windows

Vinyl Design and ProVia both fall under full frame vinyl or replacement vinyl.

**Full frame vinyl is a rule, not a judgment.** If the existing window is all
vinyl with J-channel outside and no wood anywhere, it is full frame vinyl,
always, regardless of what goes back in. Even an Andersen 100 Series.

## Two small things

You cannot delete a wrong adder. Go back into Select Existing and unclick it.

Always double check the adder count before you move on. Zero on a window we are
installing means you sold the window and gave away the labor.

modules.title: Install types
modules.body_md:
Three ways we put a window in. They have different labor, different materials,
and different prices. Choosing the wrong one on a quote is one of the few
mistakes that costs real money and is not obvious afterward.

Everything in adders depends on getting this right first.

## Replacement, also called insert or pocket

The old wood window frame stays. We take out the upper sash, the lower sash,
and the jamb liners, which are the tracks running up the sides. A smaller
window gets made to fit inside what is left.

Less labor. Less material. No exterior work in most cases.

## Full frame

The window comes out down to the wall studs. New moldings inside and out.

Much more labor and much higher material cost. This is the one people
underestimate.

## New construction

The opening is already framed and ready. We set the window, shim it plumb level
and square, caulk it, and leave. No trim work inside or out.

Significantly cheaper than either of the others. This is contractor and builder
work where someone else handles the finish. In-home sales rarely sees it. B2B
sees it regularly.

## Two traps

**The screened porch conversion.** It looks like new construction, because
there is an opening waiting for a window. But we are doing trim work and
finishing, so it is full frame. Getting this one wrong is expensive, because
new construction pricing is far below full frame.

**Existing vinyl windows.** If the existing window is all vinyl with no wood
anywhere, and there is J-channel outside with the siding tucked behind it, that
is **full frame vinyl. Always.** It does not matter what goes back in. Not an
insert, even if you are putting in an Andersen 100 Series or a ProVia or a
Vinyl Design unit. There is no wood frame to insert into.

## Quick test

Is there an existing wood frame we are leaving in place?
→ Yes: replacement. No: keep going.

Is the opening finished, or does someone else handle trim?
→ Someone else handles it and we only set the unit: new construction.
→ We are trimming it out: full frame.

options: New construction, the openings are ready
Full frame, because we are doing trim work and finishing
