quiz.q: Which install type carries the highest material cost?
options: Full frame, because of new moldings inside and out

modules.title: Adder traps
modules.body_md:
Adders are how we capture labor. Every failure below is silent. Nothing warns
you, the quote still looks finished, and the customer still signs. You find out
when the crew invoices for work nobody charged for.

Read this before you build your first quote.

## Do this first, every time

**Margin alignment factor, before you quote anything.** Project Adders, select
existing, Service Fees tab, check it, done.

It adds 11.11% so you have room to discount back down during the price
conversation. There are safeguards that should stop you dropping below the
floor, but the factor has to be in before you build, not after.

If you know the customer just wants the best number out the door and will not
negotiate, you can skip it. If there is any chance they want to feel like they
won something, put it in.

## Adders live in two different places

**Andersen windows and Andersen patio doors:** the adder is inside each line
item. Edit the window, go to the Adders tab.

**Therma-Tru via Reeb, ProVia, Vinyl Design, DSA:** adders go at the project
level, added at the end under Project Adders.

**Line level** applies to that one unit. **Project level** is one cost for the
whole job regardless of how many openings.

## The five traps

**1. The Andersen zero.** After building an Andersen line item the Adders tab
shows a count. If it reads 0 on a window we are installing, you just sold the
window and gave away the labor. Check the number is not zero before you move
on.

**2. Copy does not copy adders.** Copying a window brings across colors, glass,
hardware, grilles, everything. Not the adders. Every copied unit needs its
adders added. This is the easiest one to miss because the copy looks complete.

**3. Reeb imports at quantity 1.** The import pulls in all your doors, then the
non-Andersen door adder lands at quantity 1 no matter how many doors are on the
quote. Three doors means highlighting the 1, deleting it, and typing 3.

**4. Vinyl Design quantity means two different things.** The package adder,
which is the whole window quote as one line, stays at quantity 1. Charge it at
2 and the customer pays for the windows twice. The installation adder lines
take real counts. Casements and double hungs going into existing frames price
the same, so they collapse onto one line at the combined count. New
construction units are separate lines at their own counts.

**5. Transoms are a separate line.** On the non-Andersen doors tab, a door with
a transom needs both the door adder and the transom adder. Miss the transom and
the crew's transom labor is unbilled.

## Taxable service is not a habit, it is per source

**Vinyl Design package adder: leave it OFF.** Wake County's 7.25% is already
built into the Vinyl Design quote. Checking taxable service double-taxes the
customer.

**Change order adder: ON.** It is a taxable service.

Learn one and apply it everywhere and you will be wrong half the time.

## You cannot delete a wrong adder

Go back into select existing and unclick it. There is no delete.

## United Inches

Several adders are priced by UI. **United Inches = width + height.** A 50 by 50
window is 100 UI.

Tiers are 102 or less, 103 to 125, and over 125. Bigger and heavier means more
to the subcontractors, so the labor price steps up.

## What carpentry adders cover

These are the things the crew charges us for, so we charge for them:

Taking blinds down and rehanging them. Interior shutters, usually plantation,
which cost more than exterior. Exterior shutters. Brickmold and sill nose
replacement. Cutting windows out of an opening, which comes up with bricked-over
or old aluminum units and is more labor than it sounds. Field-cutting and
applying extension jambs. Siding repair and rot. Storm window removal.

Painting is separate and has to be discussed with the customer during the
quote, because they sign off on it in the labor contract.

modules.title: Tempered glass and code
modules.body_md:
Tempered is safety glass. It breaks like a windshield, into small squares
rather than shards, so it is far less likely to cut someone. It is also
stronger than annealed glass, so in many cases it does not break at all.

Getting this wrong is the one product mistake with real liability attached.

## Doors: always tempered, no decision to make

**All door glass is tempered by federal law.** Every manufacturer, every size,
from a small decorative lite to a full sheet. Andersen, ProVia, Therma-Tru, all
of them.

You do not select it. You do not quote it as an upgrade. It is simply always
there.

## Windows: know the triggers

Tempered is required when the glass is:

- **18 inches or less from the floor and more than 9 square feet**
- **60 inches or less above a stair, a landing, or the walking surface**
- **60 inches or less inside a shower or tub area**
- **In the path of a door that swings into it**

On a double hung, **the upper and lower sashes count separately.** One sash can
require tempering when the other does not.

## Why it matters when nobody is checking

Replacement windows do not require permits, so there is no inspector coming.
Nothing forces the issue.

Two exposures remain.

**Injury.** Someone falls on the stairs or slips in the shower and goes through
the glass. Untempered glass in those locations is exactly the scenario the code
exists to prevent.

**Resale.** An inspector during a future sale catches untempered glass where
code requires it. That is a call from a former customer two years later, and a
problem they now have to fix.

Know the code and temper where it belongs, even though nobody will check at the
time.

## Do not confuse this with window opening control devices

Different rule, different purpose. Those are about children falling out of
windows.

**Required when the window is 18 inches or less from the floor and the outside
drop is more than 60 inches.**

They screw into the window and can be factory or field applied. Most people do
not want them. Not strictly required on a replacement where no permit is
pulled, but worth offering to a family with small children.

modules.title: The Value Match Guarantee
modules.body_md:
## Say the whole thing

**Never say "price match."**

Price match invites a bare number comparison, which is exactly what the terms
exist to prevent. Say **Value Match Guarantee**, every time, because we match
what they get, not just what they pay. Getting the words right in front of a
customer is not pedantry, it is the difference between a promise we can keep
and one we cannot.

## The promise

> Buy from Window Works Co. with complete confidence. If within 30 days of
> signing you show us a written, detailed quote from another licensed, insured
> contractor for the same windows, the same installation, and the same warranty
> at a lower total price, we will refund you the difference and give you an
> extra $100.
>
> **You will never overpay buying from us.**

## Why it holds up

The refund only fires when a licensed local competitor commits **in writing**
to the identical product, the same installation method, the same air sealing
and materials, and the same warranty, at a lower total, and will confirm it on
a phone call.

A lowball quote or a big box store almost never matches all of that on paper.
The cheap version skimps on exactly the things that do not show up in a photo:
little or no foam, builder grade caulk, a shorter labor warranty. Line the two
up honestly and they stop being comparable.

When it does fire, a true equal genuinely beat us, which is rare. Paying $100
on that rare miss buys loud word of mouth, and word of mouth feeds our
returning customer business.

**These terms are honest, not a trick.** They are written so that the only
quotes that qualify are the ones that should trigger a refund.

## The eight conditions

Every one must be met. If any single condition fails, the quote is not
equivalent and the claim does not pay.

**1. Equivalent product.** Identical manufacturer, product line, series, frame
material, glass package, hardware, and interior and exterior color. Grilles
must match in construction, pattern, and bar specification. Between the glass,
simulated divided lite, and true divided lite are different products at very
different prices, so the same pattern built as a cheaper grille type does not
qualify.

**2. Equivalent installation.** Full frame to full frame, or pocket and insert
to pocket and insert. And a comparable air sealing package: minimal expansion
polyurethane foam formulated for windows and doors around the full perimeter,
since standard expanding foam bows the frame and does not qualify. A premium
exterior grade sealant, properly tooled over correct joint prep. Flashing
integration appropriate to the method. Interior and exterior trim, capping and
wrapping, and debris haul away. Builder grade acrylic caulk, unfoamed gaps, or
a stripped down job is not equivalent.

**3. Equivalent warranty.** Same or better product warranty and same or better
labor warranty term. **Ours is two years on workmanship,** so a competitor at
one year does not qualify.

**4. Same job.** Same opening count, same measured sizes and options.

**5. Licensed and insured competitor.** Licensed in North Carolina, insured for
this work, serving the area where the home is.

**6. Written and scope specific.** Signed, dated, on their letterhead, stating
the product and the full scope with a total package price. No line item
breakdown required, since we compare on total. Details a quote would not
normally list, like the specific foam or sealant, we confirm on our verification
call. Verbal quotes, texts, screenshots, and ballpark ranges do not qualify.

**7. Current timing.** Shown to us within 30 days of signing, and the quote
must state its validity period, which must still be in effect.

**8. Total to total.** Real out the door price for equivalent scope, net of any
standard discount either company offers, **including ours.** So the three day
deal, the authorized discount, the cash discount, and the referral bonus all
count against us in the comparison. Stacking discounts lowers the number a
competitor has to beat.

## Never eligible

Clearance, floor models, discontinued, liquidation, going out of business, or
employee and friends and family pricing.

Quotes containing errors or omissions, or that the issuing contractor will not
honor or verify.

Labor only or product only quotes.

Anything submitted more than 30 days after signing.

Any quote we cannot verify directly with the contractor who issued it.

## The claim process

The customer submits the written competing quote within 30 days of signing.

We verify it directly with the issuing contractor, to confirm it is real,
current, and equivalent, and to resolve any suspected error with them.

At our option we either match the price plus $100, or decline with a written
explanation of the differences.

One claim per contract, available only to the named customer, not transferable.

## Running it at the table

**It is an objection remover, not a discount.** Lead with it to close today.
Never use it to justify dropping your price.

When a customer raises a cheaper number:

**Do not flinch and do not drop your price.** The guarantee is exactly why they
can buy today with zero risk.

**Ask for the written, detailed quote** so you can line it up side by side.
This alone ends most price objections, because the comparison rarely exists on
paper.

**Walk the gaps out loud.** The foam and sealant package that actually keeps
air and water out, and the labor warranty term. Before treating any cheaper
quote as comparable, confirm it is the same product, the same installation
method, and the same materials.

**Offer to re-spec our quote down** to the lesser scope so the choice is theirs
and fully informed. Most decline once they see what they give up.

**Never promise a payout at the table.** Point to the written terms. The office
verifies and administers every claim.

modules.title: Presenting in Ingage

The software is straightforward. Four things worth knowing.

- **Load it before the appointment starts.** If you have already tapped into
  the presentation, it opens fast when you need it. Nobody should be watching a
  loading screen in their living room.

- **Blue icon, not black.** The Demo tile shows two things that look like the
  Ingage presentation. The blue one is what you present from. The black one
  with the suitcase exists only so Vendo can email the customer a link at the
  end.

- **Offline works, links do not.** Downloaded content presents fine without
  WiFi, but web link buttons and HTML pages will not load. Know which parts of
  our deck are links so you can route around them.

- **It sits on the table.** Built 4:3 for iPad, meant to face the customer on a
  counter or table, not held like a clipboard.

Ingage's own "How to Present" video is in the tech stack deck if you want it.

modules.title: Taking great pictures in CompanyCam
modules.body_md:
Three teams use your photos, and one of them is you.

**Project management and installation** need to know what they are walking
into. Damage, rot, access, anything unusual.

**Marketing** uses the exteriors.

**You** need them more than you expect. Was that a 445 or a 442? What was the
grille pattern? What hardware finish am I matching on the second phase of this
job? A photo answers it in seconds.

## Exteriors

**Level.** CompanyCam has a level tool, use it.

**All the angles in frame.** Roof edges, the peak, the chimney, both sides of
the house.

**Landscape, not portrait.** This is the one people get wrong. Portrait makes
sense for windows and doors, but exteriors are mostly for marketing, so
landscape.

**All four elevations** where you can get them safely.

## Interiors

**Ask before you turn on lights.** Then turn them back off when you are done.
Without interior light you get a silhouette against a bright window and the
photo is useless.

**Capture the entire framing** around each window and door, not just the
opening. Molding, casing, hardware, all of it in one shot.

**Document any damage.** Rot especially. If you suspect water damage in a wall
below a window, photograph it and say so. That is exactly the heads up the PM
and crew need before they arrive.

## Details worth shooting

Molding profiles. Hardware colors. Grille patterns, particularly anything
unusual, and note that a nine over one is not common. Architectural oddities
like a bump out, which tells the install team what they are dealing with.

## Do your best

Terrain, weather, pets, cars, drapes, safety, a palm tree in front of the door.
Sometimes you cannot get the shot. That is understood. Get what you can.

modules.title: 100 Series single and double hung
modules.body_md:
All Fibrex fiberglass composite. No wood anywhere, inside or out.

## The single hung

Only the bottom sash operates. The top is fixed. It does not tilt in.

It is a side load, meaning you pull clips and pop the sash out, and that is
designed for service and sash replacement rather than cleaning. It is not a
simple job.

Go feel one in the showroom. The sash moves back and forth in a way that reads
cheap even though the quality is fine. That is a design issue, not a quality
issue, and it is why this has never been a favorite.

## The double hung

Recently released and the opposite story. Both sashes operate, it tilts in for
cleaning, there is no play in the sash, and the frame is solid.

**This is the one to sell.** We expect it to become one of our top sellers over
the next decade, and it is our answer whenever someone is shopping vinyl
replacement, especially if they want black on the outside.

The field it competes in is Renewal by Andersen, Marvin Infinity, Pella, and
ProVia, all of which sit at the higher end of fiberglass.

## What Fibrex gives you

Non rot. A green product, made from recycled sawdust and wood bound with
polymer resin from fiberglass. Significantly stronger than vinyl.

Color is integral to the material rather than painted on top. Scratch a painted
vinyl window and you find a different color underneath. Scratch this and you
have to go deep before you reach anything different.

## Sizing and options

Nominal sizing, which suits replacing existing vinyl from new construction.
Custom in eighth inch increments, and it is forgiving and cost effective.

Exterior: white, Sandtone, Terratone, dark bronze, black. Two tone available.

Grilles: SDL or between the glass only. **Removable grilles are not available
on any 100 Series window.**

Hardware: always the metal slimline lock. See the never sell sheet.

modules.title: 100 Series casement and awning
modules.body_md:
Both in one module. Casements crank out right or left. Awnings crank upward
about 30 degrees, not 90, which is worth setting straight with a homeowner
before they buy one expecting full ventilation.

Either can be ordered stationary.

## Stationary casement or awning, versus a picture window

If you have several units in a row and some do not open, a stationary casement
or awning keeps the visible sash line so the whole row looks uniform from
outside. Nobody can tell which ones operate.

A picture window has no sash. The frame runs across in one piece.

Picture is less expensive, and above certain sizes casement is not available so
picture is the only option. Below that, it is a look decision.

## The casement conversion

This is a real sales play. A customer with a bank of old wood double hungs can
go back with 100 Series casements as inserts and completely change the look of
the house at a reasonable price.

The 100 Series is the line for this, because its eighth inch custom sizing is
cheap and forgiving. On the 400 Series the same conversion costs considerably
more.

## Details

Same Fibrex, same glass packages, same colors as the rest of the 100 Series.

Screens: fiberglass mesh is the less expensive option, TruScene is available.
Casements only ever take a full screen.

Awnings get a lock on both sides. Casements get one, in the lower corner, with
folding hardware.

modules.title: 100 Series gliding windows
modules.body_md:
**If you are selling a gliding window at Window Works, this is almost certainly
the one.** Across every brand and every line we carry, this is the go to.

One panel slides, the other is fixed. **You choose the operating side viewed
from the exterior.** Unlike a double casement you cannot open both.

## Why it wins

Fibrex lets it go bigger than vinyl. Six by six on a double, and triples run to
roughly twelve feet.

**Screened porch conversions are where we sell the most of them.** Those
openings are whatever someone framed years ago, with no standard sizing, and
this window customizes to fit. Pair it with 100 Series casements and picture
windows to fill a whole run.

The real advantage on a porch is space. Casements crank out into wherever people
are walking or sitting. Gliders do not take any space at all, so a patio, a set
of stairs, or a table and chairs stays usable.

Also works as a pass through from a kitchen to a porch or patio, at a fraction
of what a multi glide or bifold would cost.

Available without a nailing flange, so it can go in as an insert where a
picture window was, or where two double hungs come out and the divider between
them goes with them.

## Easy Breeze

The competitor you will meet on porch conversions. Local contractors and
dealers push it hard in the Triangle.

It is a vinyl triple track system, and the panel is vinyl too. Not glass. It is
plastic and you can press on it.

For a four season room where the customer wants real heating and cooling
performance, this is not close. Spend a few minutes on their website so you can
speak to it accurately rather than just dismissing it.

## Hardware

Slimline metal, always, about five to ten dollars per window. We do not ask, we
just include it. Plastic breaks.

modules.title: 100 Series gliding door
modules.body_md:
Our budget gliding patio door, and a good one.

Fibrex, non rot, priced right around vinyl and sometimes under ProVia. Well
below the 200, 400, E and A Series.

## Fibrex versus vinyl, and this is where it matters most

**Fibrex is 2.5 times stronger than vinyl.** If you are going to make that
comparison anywhere, make it here.

Vinyl gliding doors get problematic over time. The glass panels are heavy and
plastic framing struggles to carry that weight, so you get warping and
operation problems as the panel presses into the frame. Fibrex carries it.

Be fair about the exception: ProVia puts steel reinforcing in their door
panels, which helps a great deal. Not all vinyl is equal, and saying so makes
you more credible, not less.

The cheap gliding doors at a big box store are a different matter. That is
where the real problems come from.

## What it is and is not

**Two panel only.** No four panel option in the 100 Series.

One panel operates, the other is fixed. **Choose the operating side from the
exterior.**

**It cannot be ordered knockdown.** The frame is integrally built and does not
screw together in the field. This is the opposite of the 400 Series rule, so do
not promise a customer a knockdown delivery on this door. It makes transport
harder, and that is the tradeoff for the price.

## Details

Sizes from about five feet, six standard, up to eight feet tall, customizable.

Hardware is limited. Tulsa in white, Sandtone, or black. Afton if they want
satin nickel, bright brass, antique brass, or black. Both metal.

**Auxiliary foot lock, about fifteen dollars, always included.** Slightly
different design from the 400 Series version but it does the same job.

Screens: fiberglass mesh only. **TruScene is not available on doors, it is
considered a hazard.** Standard sliding screen panel.

Same glass options as the rest of the line.

## Showroom

We do not have one on display, but there are corner sections so you can show a
customer the sill. Go look at them.

modules.title: 100 Series picture and specialty
modules.body_md:
Picture windows are most of what you will sell here. Specialty shapes are
available but limited.

## The frame rule, and it applies to the whole 100 Series

**The frame is 3-1/4 inches per side.** That means 6-1/2 inches of any unit
dimension is frame, in both directions.

A 12 by 12 picture window leaves you 5-1/2 inches of glass. It does not look
good.

We learned this the hard way. A customer was warned, insisted, saw the window at
pickup, and wanted to return it. Once it is ordered, we own it and they own it.

So on anything small, a walk in closet, a short wide unit, look at a specialty
window instead. The rule holds across the gliders, single hung, and casements
too. The smaller the unit, the more pronounced the frame.

## Where picture windows work

Big sizes are excellent. Up to six by eight, because Fibrex carries it. Down to
one by one, eighth inch increments, customizable.

**Screened porch conversions,** filling openings alongside the gliding windows.

**Living rooms** where a customer has a bank of old wood double hungs and tells
you they never open them anyway. Converting to energy efficient picture windows
is a nicer look and we have done plenty.

**Never in a bedroom.** Bedrooms require egress. It is not grandfathered. If
you convert the only operable window in a bedroom you have created a code
violation and a safety problem.

## What it looks like

No sash. The frame runs across in one piece. Compare that with a stationary
casement or awning, which keeps the sash line. In a row of units that
difference shows.

No welded sash corner either, so you get a clean miter with none of the rough
edges you see on a vinyl window. Look at both in the showroom.

## Specialty shapes

Trapezoids, half circles, and so on are available in the 100 Series, but the
thick frame works against them. Small sizes lose most of their glass, and
lining up angles for a roofline is harder with a heavy profile.

For most architectural shapes, Andersen specialty or E-Series is the better
answer. Less expensive here, but more limited and it will not look as good.

modules.title: 400 Series Tilt Wash double hung
modules.body_md:
One of two double hungs in the 400 Series. The other is the Woodwright, and
they are different windows. **Always say Tilt Wash or Woodwright, never "400
Series double hung."** The shared name confuses customers, contractors, and
everyone else.

Andersen's workhorse. Mid tier: above their lower lines, below the upper ones.
One of our top sellers as a full frame application, and easy to service because
it comes apart and back together cleanly.

## Construction

Wood frame, wood interior, unfinished pine. Vinyl clad on the frame and sashes.
Fibrex composite sill with a 14 degree pitch, which is standard for old wood
windows.

## Why it sells

**Stock sizes match traditional wood window sizes.** Full frame tear out to the
studs and no customization needed.

That keeps the continuity of the home's look, limits siding and exterior work,
and if you go back with the same size molding inside you usually avoid paint
lines. Not guaranteed, and it is not in our labor contract, but usually.

Both sashes tilt in, though it is harder than on the upper lines because there
is no tilt latch built into the lock.

## Config traps

**Custom sizing exists in eighth inch increments and will price you out of the
deal.** On an old wood window you almost certainly do not need it.

**Black or dark bronze interiors are only available matching the same
exterior.** Black outside allows black or white inside. Dark bronze allows dark
bronze or white. White outside with black inside is not available on this
window, though Andersen allows it on other lines.

**No factory stain.** Unfinished pine only. Someone else stains it after.

## Never sell

**Optional lift hardware.** Andersen moved framing up for energy performance
and it no longer lines up, sitting above the glass. They still sell it. We sold
expensive bright brass hand lifts to a customer who chose the window for them
and then could not fit them. Fine on the Woodwright, never here.

## Details

Hardware: standard locking keeper in white, stone, or black, all metal. Estate
locking keeper for antique brass, bright brass, distressed bronze, satin
nickel. Estate comes up most in kitchens where someone is matching cabinet
hardware.

Exterior: seven colors. White is 75 to 80 percent of what you sell, black
second. Terratone and forest green show up in wooded and rural settings.

Trim: Andersen's is Fibrex and it is nice when it works, but the spacing fails
in brick openings. We use PVC brickmold, and white PVC matches Andersen white
closely enough that most people do not paint it.

Product ID `TW`, then sash size. `TW2636` is 2 feet 6 by 3 feet 6.

modules.title: 400 Series Woodwright double hung
modules.body_md:
The other 400 Series double hung, and a step above the Tilt Wash.

## Why they share a name

When both launched the frame was essentially the same: same PVC wrap on the
upper frame, same Fibrex sill, both sized to replace old wood windows. They
have diverged since, and the sashes were always different.

Which is why you never say "400 Series double hung" to anybody.

## What makes it the upgrade

**Architecturally correct sash.** Go into a colonial home or up into New
England and the old wood sashes look like this.

**More wood.** Wood jamb liners, where the Tilt Wash uses PVC. That is where
the name comes from.

**All Fibrex sash exterior** rather than vinyl clad, which gives it a more
beveled, cleaner profile.

**Easy tilt release.** The tilt mechanism is built into the lock. Unlock, keep
turning, and the lower sash disengages. Top sash has tilt pins.

**Wood species options.** Unfinished pine, maple, or oak. Still no factory
stain.

## Same as the Tilt Wash

Sash sizing, so the same full frame pitch applies: tear out to the studs, no
customizing, keeps the look, limits siding and interior work. Same caveat about
paint lines not being guaranteed.

Same exterior colors, same glass options, same trim limitations, so PVC
brickmold again.

## Different from the Tilt Wash

**Hand lifts work fine here.** Sell them if the customer wants them. This is
the opposite of the Tilt Wash rule and it catches people.

**No estate hardware.** Discontinued long ago. Easy tilt release is the only
style, though you can pick finishes. If a customer has old Woodwright windows
and wants to match the old hardware for continuity, it can be special quoted.

## Product ID

`WDH` plus sash size. `WDH3442` is 3 feet 4 by 4 feet 2. Unit dimensions run
larger because of the frame.

One measuring note: stated height runs from the top of the frame to the very
bottom of the sloped sill, so the interior sits a little higher than the number
suggests.

modules.title: 400 Series casement
modules.body_md:
One casement in the 400 Series. Unlike the double hungs there are no variants.

Crank out, right or left. Can be ordered stationary, which comes up on a three
panel where the centre does not open.

## Construction

Vinyl clad over a pine frame, wrapped 360 degrees including the sash and sealed
inside the vinyl. Non rot, with the strength and rigidity of real wood behind
it.

Painted interiors are a baked on polyurethane rubber base paint, so no
brushstrokes. That holds across the painted Andersen line.

## The extension jamb question

This is the thing to check in the house.

Tilt Wash and Woodwright frames are 4-9/16 deep and reach the interior
sheetrock flush on a 2x4 wall. **Casement framing is narrow and does not.**

So either you add extension jambs, available factory or field applied, or the
house already has sheetrock returns. Look before you quote. Field applied
jambs are a carpentry adder, so it matters twice.

## Sizing

Casements do not match old wood double hung openings, so a full frame
conversion almost always means customizing. Stock sizing exists and is worth
checking anyway, because occasionally you get lucky.

Custom costs more, same as the double hungs.

## The kitchen sink play

Even in a house full of double hungs, people often want one casement behind the
sink. Cranking beats reaching across the counter to lift a sash.

Pair it with estate hardware matching their cabinet finishes and you have a
specific, high value recommendation you can make in almost every kitchen.

## Details

Grilles are rarer here. One sheet of glass, and most people want the view.

Seven exterior colors, same as the rest of the 400. White leads, but black is
climbing on casements, especially on contemporary homes or a house doing
casements throughout.

Traditional versus contemporary profile differs only in the interior glass
stops. Hard to see on the website, clearer in the quoting schematic.

Product ID starts with `C`. The numbers after it are Andersen's own designation
with no sash or nominal logic, so do not try to decode them.

modules.title: 400 Series awning
modules.body_md:
Andersen's best selling awning, though we do not sell many in this market. Know
enough to quote one.

Vinyl clad, wood framed, wood interior. Slim profile, which suits contemporary
homes.

## The 30 degree fact

Homeowners assume an awning cranks up to 90 degrees. **It goes about 30.**

So ventilation is limited. Set that expectation before they buy one, not after.

## Frame depth

**2-1/8 inches.** Even shallower than the casement, so extension jambs or
sheetrock returns are effectively required on a 2x4 wall.

Across the 400 Series: double hungs reach the interior, casements and awnings
do not.

## The sizing chart trap

Width and height ranges do not combine freely. Seeing 35-15/16 to 71-7/8 on
width does not mean you can pair the widest width with a 48 inch height. The
crank up geometry rules out certain combinations.

Check the chart rather than assuming a rectangle of valid sizes, or you will
submit something that comes back rejected.

## Profile consistency

If a house mixes awnings and casements, keep contemporary or traditional
consistent across all of them. They share a profile family and mismatching
looks wrong.

## Details

Interior colors are limited by exterior, same as the Tilt Wash. Black outside
allows black or white inside, dark bronze allows dark bronze or white, and
white outside with black inside is not available.

Unfinished pine or prefinished white. No wood species upgrades and no factory
stain.

Hardware matches the casements. Contemporary folding, white, stone, or black
standard, with bright brass, distressed bronze, satin nickel, or oil rubbed
bronze as upgrades. Oil rubbed bronze is often written or spoken as ORB.

Product ID starts with `A`. The numbers after do not decode.

modules.title: 400 Series picture windows
modules.body_md:
A picture window does not open. Usually square, sometimes rectangular, often
large.

## There are three of them

This is the part the website does not show you, and it only appears in the
quoting software.

The 400 Series has a picture window profile for each partner line:

- One to match the **Tilt Wash**, with a sloped sill and a vinyl clad surround
- One to match the **Woodwright**, sloped sill and Fibrex surround
- One to match the **casement and awning**, which share a profile

Match the picture window to the line the customer chose. Put the wrong one in a
row of Tilt Wash and the elevation looks wrong.

## The color rule, and it is worth knowing across every line

**Andersen white is the same white on every series, every style, every cladding
material.** Same for black, dark bronze, Sandtone, Terratone.

So you can mix aluminum clad, vinyl clad, and Fibrex in one house and the
colors match. That is a genuine selling point when someone is combining
E-Series with 400, or adding 100 Series gliders to a porch.

## Sizing

**Picture windows do not follow traditional wood window sizes.** Replacing an
old wood picture window means customizing, every time.

Note that this contradicts the Tilt Wash pitch, where matching wood sizes is
the whole argument. Within the 400 Series: double hungs match, casements do
not, picture windows do not.

## Details

Same interior and exterior colors, grille patterns, trim options, and glass as
the rest of the 400.

Product ID starts with `P`. A contemporary `P3535` is the casement and awning
profile.

modules.title: 400 Series specialty windows
modules.body_md:
Short one. Awareness rather than depth.

Andersen makes a very wide range of shapes: ovals, circles, trapezoids, arches,
eyebrows which are short arches, triangles including right and isosceles.
Single units, or configured as multiple staged windows.

Available across essentially all their lines, some better than others.

## Specialty is not only fancy shapes

The specialty division also handles custom sized square and rectangular picture
windows, and transoms above a window, in sizes the regular lines will not
build.

That reframe matters. "Specialty" sounds exotic and most of the time it just
means a size the standard catalog cannot do.

## What a rep should take from this

Walking into a house and seeing an odd window is not an automatic no. Andersen
probably has it, or can create it, usually as a custom or special order.

You likely will not be able to price it on the spot. That is fine. Recognize
it, tell the customer we can almost certainly do it, and hand it off.

This is the same situation as big doors and Reeb custom doors. Three different
products, one procedure.

## Design rule

On anything angled, follow the roof line. Separate from any trend report, it
simply looks wrong when it does not.

modules.title: 400 Series patio doors, hinged and gliding
modules.body_md:
Both in one module.

## All door glass is tempered

Federal law. Every manufacturer, every size, from a small lite to a full sheet.
You do not select it and you do not quote it as an upgrade. See the tempered
glass reference sheet.

## Andersen undersizes doors

**Their 6'8" is 79.5 inches. Doors in the field are around 82.**

For a standard 6'8" opening you need the **6'11" option, 82-3/8**.

The cause is a measuring convention. Door companies quote the panel and add the
frame. Andersen gives you the whole product including frame. Select 6'8"
because the existing door is a 6'8" and it will not fit.

## Hinged, the French wood door

Double or single, full lite, traditional profile with more wood around the
glass.

**The multi-point lock is the best in the industry.** Deadbolt locks the entire
handle set so you cannot lift or push the handle. And Andersen builds the
active and passive panel activation into the hardware, so there is no astragal
with flip levers to fumble with. Push either handle and both panels operate.

Worth contrasting with Therma-Tru, whose multi-point we will not sell because
it fails. Andersen builds in house. Therma-Tru ships to distributors who
assemble. Same feature, opposite verdict, and that contrast explains our whole
brand position.

The 400 Series hinged door is frozen in time. The A-Series looks nearly
identical with far more options. This one still works well, but colors and
options are limited.

**Adjustable hinges.** You can raise, lower, or shift the panel. That matters
here because our clay soil keeps houses moving for 40 to 50 years, so a door
that goes out of reveal can be brought back rather than replaced.

## Gliding, the French wood glider

Traditional thick lower panels, ball bearing roller track.

**Raised track, almost like a monorail,** so dirt and debris fall away instead
of jamming the rollers the way recessed tracks used to.

**Roller adjustment with a Phillips head** from the inside, same reasoning as
the hinges.

200 and 400 Series gliders share the same frame, rollers, and hardware. Only
the panel profile differs.

Standard width 71.25, and gliders go much larger than hinged doors because the
support system is different. Up to what they call 8 foot, actual unit 95-1/4,
and 8 foot in height.

C handle, standard across most brands.

## Two rules

**Order knockdown, always.** Safer to handle, less damage, one person can
deliver it, and there is a small price break. Our crews assemble in 15 to 20
minutes. We do not offer assembled. Note the 100 Series glider cannot be
ordered this way.

**Include the auxiliary foot lock, always, without asking.** Thirty to
thirty five dollars. A real deadbolt shoot bolt operated with your foot, and it
can be drilled for a second position so the door locks while vented.

## Hardware finishes are style specific

Not a universal palette. Albany is white, black, stone only. Tribeca is white
or stone. Anvers gets satin nickel, bright brass, ORB. FSB is stainless only.
Ashley Norton has the widest range. Names correspond across hinged and gliding.
Every style and every finish is a different price.

## Blinds between the glass

Available on stock sizes, lost if you customize. Excellent for kids and pets
because they cannot be damaged, and they never need cleaning since they are
sealed in.

## Pro tip that applies everywhere

The website and the quoting software disagree, and neither is reliably current.
**Check quoting.**

## Product IDs

`FWG` French wood glider. `FWI` in swing hinged, `FWO` out swing. Out swing is
discontinued but still shows on the website.

modules.title: Quoting Therma-Tru doors in Reeb 2G
modules.body_md:
Reeb is the distributor we buy Therma-Tru doors from, and Reeb 2G is their
quoting software. Keep it on your iPad home screen.

## How Therma-Tru actually works, and why it matters

Therma-Tru manufactures fiberglass door panels and door slabs and ships them to
distributors around the country. **The distributor assembles the door in the
frame and hangs it, in their own shop.** They also do the prefinishing.

So quality varies by distributor. Reeb is good, and does a nice job on
prefinishes. Others in the area over the years have not been.

Contrast that with Andersen and ProVia, who build everything in house and ship
on their own logistics.

Most people assume a Therma-Tru door is built by Therma-Tru, whether they buy
it from us or a big box store. It is not. Worth understanding, because it is
also why we do not sell their multi-point lock.

## Getting around

Projects to reopen an existing quote. Start a new quote, then Go.

Reeb carries a lot of building supply products. **We generally sell only their
Therma-Tru doors.** Exception: residential fire doors, if someone needs a
20 minute fire rated door from the house to the garage.

Exterior Doors is where you are going.

## Choosing a line

Classic Craft, Fiber Classic, and Smooth Star all have a composite edge, with
no wood exposed to the elements. **Those are the three.**

Reeb also offers wood doors and their own economy fiberglass, which is a
Therma-Tru with a wood edge. **Never.** It rots in our humidity, and we have
seen them fail in as little as twelve months.

## Everything is viewed from the exterior

**Critical.** Configuration, especially sidelights.

Standing outside, the sidelight on the right is a right sidelight. Pick it
from the inside and the customer gets a door with the sidelight on the wrong
side.

Even when you are standing inside the house thinking about it, it is the
opposite of what you are looking at.

## Working through the build

Entry versus hinged patio versus fixed. Then configuration: single, single with
sidelights, transoms, double.

**Widths are the slab, not the finished unit.** A 28, 30, or 34 is the door
panel. You still account for the frame. Heights are usually 6'8" or 8'0".

Panel style, flat or raised, glass options, grille patterns and whether
composite or aluminum SDL.

**Colors.** Reeb's own palette, Therma-Tru Prismaguard, or Sherwin Williams
color match. Sherwin Williams costs more, but it removes all the back and
forth. You just need the color number. And if a customer is torn between two
colors, pick one to close the deal. Pricing is identical and we can edit it
later.

Exterior and interior are separate, so two tone is easy.

**Handing.** In swing or out swing, left or right. Match the existing swing
unless they specifically want a change. Ninety plus percent do not. But when a
door swings into a tight space, changing it can transform the room, and that is
worth raising.

**Brickmold.** Standard or flat casing, check what they have. **Always Frame
Saver, never On Guard.** Shipped loose is usually no, occasionally yes on brick
or rock work so the installers can adjust.

**Hinges.** Standard radius by square almost always. Ball bearing, self
closing, and adjustable are upgrades.

**Jamb depth.** 4-9/16 for 2x4, 6-9/16 for 2x6, 9-1/4 for very thick walls.
**Cannot be changed in the field.** Get it wrong and the door is reordered.

**Sill.** Composite adjustable, always. Never hardwood adjustable, which still
rots eventually. Never value composite. Sill horns are rare. Bronze finish only
comes with a dark cap.

**The ADA sill** is worth raising with a customer in a wheelchair, an older
customer, or anyone with mobility issues. Lower and flatter, far easier to
cross, and the standard composite sill is a trip hazard for some people. That
is a real conversation about making their home safer, not an upsell.

**Locks.** Never the Therma-Tru multi-point. Entry lock, single or double bore.
Two and three eighths back set, which is what most hardware at Lowe's or Home
Depot fits. Yes to strike jamb prep, Schlage Baldwin standard.

Weather stripping to suit the door color.

**Accessories.** Kick plate and peephole rarely. **Sill cover, always yes,** a
couple of dollars and it protects the door in transit. **Sill pan, always no,**
Reeb's is wildly overpriced and we source locally.

## Pricing

Actions, then pricing template, then **homeowner pricing.** Do not touch price
adjustment.

The lock symbol reveals cost, list, price, and margin. **Do not have that on
screen in front of a customer.**

**This price does not include labor.** Labor comes in as adders once you import
to Vendo.

## Editing

The description and the blue text on the side are all hyperlinks back into that
part of the build. Some changes force you back through later questions, some do
not.

## Adding more doors

Add, and work through again. Everything saves under one quote number.

**Note the quote ID.** You need it to import into Vendo.

## Not in the quoting system

If a customer wants something from the catalog that Reeb 2G will not build, you
can submit to find out about pricing and availability. That is a separate
process and not something you resolve at the table.

modules.title: Quoting a custom door in Reeb 2G
modules.body_md:
## Why this comes up more than you would think

**Therma-Tru has close to 5,000 door options in their catalog.** Reeb 2G only
carries part of that, mostly the popular configurations and the things they
keep in stock.

So when a customer picks something you cannot find, it usually is not that the
door does not exist. It is that the quoting software does not cover it. That
needs a special order.

## Timing

**24 to 48 hours**, usually toward the faster end. Longer if Reeb has to check
with their own suppliers on pricing or availability.

You cannot price it at the table. You can tell the customer exactly when they
will hear back, which is a much better answer than "let me look into it."

## Submitting

Log in, start a new quote. You will see the same screen as always, exterior
doors, interior doors, and so on. Scroll down to **Special Order.**

It is an order by description. A free text box, and you can drag the corner to
make it bigger.

## Write it like they cannot see what you are picturing

**This is the whole job.** Reeb does not like leaving anything open to
interpretation, and **if you do not include something, they will not include
it.**

A complete description looks like this:

> Therma-Tru Fiber Classic, FCM60 standard six panel solid, 3.0 by 6.8, 1 inch
> cut down, standard 2-3/8 double bore, strike jamb prep, bronze composite
> adjustable sill, ORB hinges, 7-1/2 inch Frame Saver jambs, right hand in
> swing, bronze weather stripping.

Note what is in there. Line, model, size, every modification, every finish, and
the handing. ORB is fine, they know it means oil rubbed bronze.

Custom jamb depths are one of the things special order can do. The 7-1/2 inch
in that example would be for an unusual masonry opening, and it is exactly the
kind of thing Reeb 2G will not build on its own.

Forget something obvious and they will email you back asking. That is not a
disaster, but it restarts the clock.

## The editing trap

Once you have saved the description, the text becomes a hyperlink. **Clicking
that hyperlink to edit will erase everything you typed.**

**Cut and paste your description somewhere safe before you click into it.**
Then paste it back and make your edits. Annoying, but that is how it behaves.

## Sending it

You need a PO number and a job name before you can submit. Fill those in and
check the marker to save.

**Project Actions**, then **Send for Special Order Review**, then Send, then
Yes.

The quote locks. You cannot touch it while Reeb is working on it, and an
eyeball icon shows they have it. You get an email when it comes back.

## When it comes back

Projects, top right. Your quote will be there with a list price on it.

Click the hyperlink and you get two options: **No, let me edit further**, or
**Yes, I accept.**

**Before you accept, compare the two sides.** The left is what you sent. The
right is what they came back with.

This is the part that matters. Read every line. They can add things, drop
things, or misinterpret something you thought was obvious. It has taken several
resubmittals on occasion, and sometimes you have to get on the phone with them.

If something is unclear, ask. You, your supervisor, or the project manager can
reach out to Reeb for clarification. Whatever we order needs to be
unambiguous.

If you need changes, choose edit further and type them in the same kind of box.

## Pricing it

Accepting does not price it for the customer. **You still have to apply the
homeowner pricing template**, the same as any other Reeb quote.

In the video: cost was $1,078 and the list came back at $2,157, so the
homeowner price lands where it should.

Then it is ready to order.

quiz.q: A customer picks a Therma-Tru door you cannot find anywhere in Reeb 2G. What does that most likely mean?
options: Therma-Tru has around 5,000 catalog options and Reeb 2G only carries part of them. It needs a special order.
You are looking in the wrong product category
Reeb does not distribute that line

quiz.q: What is the single most important thing about the description you submit?
options: Keeping it short so they can read it quickly
Being extremely specific. If you do not include something, they will not include it.

quiz.q: You saved your description and now need to change one detail. What do you do first?
options: Click the hyperlink and edit it
Cut and paste the description somewhere safe first, because clicking the hyperlink erases everything you typed

quiz.q: Reeb sends the quote back. What do you do before accepting?
options: Accept it, they are the experts
Compare what you sent against what they returned, line by line
Send it to the customer for approval

quiz.q: You accepted the returned quote. Is it ready to present to the customer?
options: Not yet. You still have to apply the homeowner pricing template.
Not yet, it needs a second approval from Reeb
Yes, once you add the labor adder in Vendo

modules.title: Importing a Reeb quote into Vendo
modules.body_md:
Short one. Reeb and ProVia both built integrations with Vendo, so this is a
proper import rather than a workaround.

## The steps

In Vendo, Configure, then the Reeb tab, then the plus sign.

**It may ask you to log in.** It will log you out eventually, so have your Reeb
credentials with you in the field. Nothing worse than being unable to import in
front of a customer.

Copy the quote ID from Reeb 2G. Paste it into Import Reeb 2G Order. Find.

Your doors pull in.

## It imports pricing, not labor

**This is the part that matters.** The import brings across the door pricing
only. The labor lives on the Vendo side and you have to add it.

Project Adders, plus, Select Existing, **non-Andersen doors** tab. That tab
covers ProVia, Reeb, and DSA, anything not built directly into Vendo the way
Andersen is.

Pick the configuration that matches. Single, double, triple, with transom, with
sidelights.

## Then fix the quantity

**The adder lands at quantity 1 regardless of how many doors are on the
quote.**

Three doors means highlighting the 1, deleting it, and typing 3.

This is one of the four adder traps and it is silent. Nothing warns you.
modules.author_note:
The video references ProVia import as already covered. It is
not, and ProVia has no training at all yet.

modules.title: Quoting Vinyl Design on the iPad
modules.body_md:
Our vinyl option. Keep the login on your home screen.

## The portal

The home screen shows company quotes, not just yours. Orders at the top are
placed orders or special quotes. Company Quotes below shows the ten most recent
across everyone. Search is in the hamburger menu if you need an older one.

Create Quote is where you start.

## Setting up

**Customer is always Window Works Company.** Ignore everything else on the
list.

Under Quote, you only need the **PO number and customer reference number.**
Nothing else on that screen.

Under Sales, your name should be populated. **Gross profit margin is manual and
does not prepopulate. For in-home sales it is 50 percent, always.** We do not
go below it. Discounts and promotions come later in Vendo.

Add, and you have a live quote with a number.

## What we sell

Vinyl Design sells trim coil, roofing, and plenty else. **We sell only their
window line.**

**Mountain View series, almost exclusively.** If a customer insists on meeting
Energy Star, you have to go to Ultra View, their newest line. For practical
purposes it is a Mountain View with tweaks to hit the new values, and it costs
more. Mountain View is already a very energy efficient window, so you are not
selling anyone short.

## The insert deduction

For an insert into an existing wood frame:

**5/8 inch off the width. 1/2 inch off the height.**

A 28 by 54 opening becomes 27-5/8 by 53-1/2. Fractions or decimals both work.

## Building a window

Quantity defaults to 1. Ignore call size and thickness, neither is relevant.

**Line item comment is worth using.** Put the room in. It prints on the label
stuck to each window, which helps the project manager and installers find where
things go without a tape measure.

**Construction type defaults to Replacement and that is almost always right.**
New construction comes with a nailing flange and different options. **Ignore
Configured in Sunroom Designer entirely.**

Finish size means exactly what you entered, tip to tip.

**Blue white is a bright white, not blue.** People do ask. Cream white is the
close match to Andersen white, which matters if a house is mixing brands. Cream
white with black laminate is a black exterior.

**No exterior painting.** We do not offer it and it is not a good product.

Custom meeting rail: none. Glass: double pane, double strength, always. Argon,
not krypton. Standard Low-E out of the box, which is already efficient, with
upgrade adders available.

**Triple pane** is very expensive for minimal gain in this market. Competitors
push it. Quote it if they insist, but try to talk them out of it.

**Tempered** where code requires it. See the tempered glass reference sheet.

Obscure or reeded glass for bathrooms, an upcharge, and worth offering where
there is a picture window near a tub.

**Grilles are vertical by horizontal, which is backwards from Andersen.** 2V 1H
is a six over six. Contour or flat, colonial or prairie. Two tone grille colors
if the exterior is dark.

**Half screen with the Better View extruded option, always.** The fiberglass
screen saves a couple of dollars and is not well made.

Locks default to single or double based on width. Flip locks are an upgrade
worth mentioning for children's rooms, since the window locks automatically
when closed.

**Insulated frame** is a small upcharge for a little more efficiency, worth
offering. **Foam wrap is automatic** and gives you the airtight fit.

**Head expander and sill expander must be added or they do not ship.** The sill
expander in particular is what finishes the outside properly.

## New construction differences

Extension jambs become relevant. Their poplar is raw, unfinished, expensive at
50 to 75 dollars a window, and honestly not great. **Better to have our crew
apply them,** or let a contractor buy their own wood. Quote it if a customer
pushes.

**Nailing fin: leave it unchecked, always.** It acts as flashing and is proper
for installation. It can be cut off in the field if needed, but it cannot be
added back.

J-channel is for vinyl siding. It can be removed in the field easily, but not
added, so think about whether it is needed.

## Twin and mulled units

Slightly different flow. Overall width and height of the whole unit, then
factory mull, then work through the rest.

## Finishing

Surcharge should always be zero. Tax is prepopulated at 7.25 percent for Wake
County.

**For the customer, print Quote Without Pricing.** That gives them all the
specifications, quantities, sizes, and the schematics on the back page, with no
prices. That is what you send. The full priced version is internal.

modules.title: Importing a Vinyl Design quote into Vendo
modules.body_md:
**Vinyl Design is the exception.** Andersen, ProVia Entry Link, and Reeb 2G all
integrate with Vendo. Vinyl Design does not, so this is a manual workaround.

It is not pretty but it works, and you need it so the quote carries the
contracts, the installation pricing, adders, discounts, and financing.

## What you need from Vinyl Design

Two things: **the quote number and the total.**

## In Vendo

Flip your screen, Vendo does not rotate.

Configure, then Project Adders top right, plus, **Create New.**

**Name** it the customer name or PO.

**Description: the quote number goes first.** Not optional.

Two people downstream depend on it. The project manager going out for the final
measure needs to know which windows they are measuring. The purchasing agent
placing the order needs to be certain they are ordering the right quote and not
another house's windows.

After the number, a rough line count with install types. "2 DH insert, 1
casement insert, 1 DH new construction, 1 twin DH new construction." That is
enough.

**Price** is the Vinyl Design total.

**Quantity stays 1.** This is the whole package as one line. Set it to 2 and
the customer pays for their windows twice.

**Taxable service: OFF.** Vinyl Design already includes Wake County's 7.25
percent. Checking it double taxes the customer.

Save.

## Then the labor

Select Existing, **Vinyl Design installation** tab. Pick the unit types. One
pass brings them all over.

**Then fix the quantities, and this is the subtle part.**

Casements and double hungs going into existing frames price the same, so they
**collapse onto one line at the combined count.** Two DH inserts plus one
casement insert is a single line at quantity 3.

New construction units are **separate lines at their own counts.**

Five windows on the quote becomes three adder lines.

## Quantity means two different things here

The package adder stays at 1 deliberately. The installation adder lines take
real counts. Both facts live in this one process and it is easy to cross them.

## Finishing

Finish, then Quote. Promotions, financing, and deposits are identical to every
other product.

**The Vendo output is ugly for Vinyl Design** because there is no real
integration, so no schematics. Send the customer the no-pricing PDF from Vinyl
Design so they can actually see what they are buying.

modules.title: Completing a change order in Vendo
modules.body_md:
A change order adds work to a job that is already sold. Rot found at measure, a
spouse who wants a second door, trim work the crew flagged.

## The one rule that matters most

**A change order adds work.** It cannot change materials and it cannot change
the products being installed. If the customer wants a different window than the
one on the signed order, that is not a change order. Stop and talk to the
office.

## The sequence

Vendo, add a new appointment. Find the customer, they are already in the system
because you quoted them. Additional contact if someone needs to sign who was
not on the original.

Confirm the address. Start time defaults to the next hour and does not matter
as long as it is that day. You can start early.

Save. **A clock icon appears.** That is how you pull information forward.

Click it, choose **change order appointment**, not sales appointment. Pick the
quote, confirm the original sales data carries over.

## Pricing the work

Configured screen, plus in the lower right, **product adders.** Any project
level adders from the original deal show here.

Plus, then **create new.** Name it change order. Write a real description:
"rot and repair of dining room, front elevation windows," not "extra work."

**Price is the crew price plus your markup**, entered as the marked up Window
Works price. Quantity 1.

**Taxable service: no.** Tax applies to products, not labor.

Save, then Finish. The quoting card turns blue.

## Quoting

No promotions, this is not a sales appointment.

If they financed the original, leave their financing selected. If they paid
cash, click out so it sits blank. **Blank means cash.**

Check pricing details to confirm the new item landed correctly against the
previous deal.

## The form

Proceed. You will see **decline installation agreement. Ignore it,** it is a
non-required form you will never use here.

Open the **change order form.** Name and address prefill. You fill **scope of
agreed upon work** and **total price.** Write the scope in real detail. One
page, that is the whole document.

## Signature

On this device right now is fastest. Personal device sends an email link.

Hand them the iPad. Start to review, agree to the electronic signature consent,
which carries the same weight as a fully executed contract. Typed or drawn,
both fine.

If they refuse consent you have a problem. Paper is a last resort and not
ideal. Work through the objection.

They complete, hand it back, you hit proceed.

## Sending

**Only the change order.** Not the Ingage presentation, not the inspection
report. The pre-selected option is already right.

Done, Next, Finish. The email is pre-written and includes their signed
document.

modules.title: Sizing conventions
modules.body_md:
Six different systems. Each one belongs to a different product or process, and
mixing them up produces a window that does not fit. Most of these mistakes are
not fixable in the field. They are reorders.

## 1. Sash size

**Andersen 400 Series Tilt Wash and Woodwright.** Also how old wood windows
were measured.

You measure the sash, not the opening. Width across the sash, height from where
the upper sash meets the lower sash down to the bottom.

`TW2636` is a Tilt Wash, 2 feet 6 inches by 3 feet 6 inches.
`WDH3442` is a Woodwright, 3 feet 4 inches by 4 feet 2 inches.

The **unit dimension** is larger than the sash size, because the frame adds
roughly three quarters of an inch. The **rough opening** is larger still,
leaving room for shims and insulation.

On both double hungs, stated height runs from the top of the frame to the very
bottom of the sloped sill, so the interior sits a little higher.

## 2. Nominal

**Vinyl windows, Andersen 100 Series, Andersen 200 Series.**

Different from sash size. This is why the 100 Series works well replacing
existing vinyl from new construction, and why the 200 Series is mostly a new
construction product: its nominal sizing cannot be customized.

## 3. United Inches

**Adders only.** Width plus height. Tiers at 102 or less, 103 to 125, and over
125. See the adder traps sheet.

## 4. Vinyl Design insert deductions

Doing an insert into an existing wood frame, deduct from the opening:

- **5/8 inch on the width**
- **1/2 inch on the height**

A 28 by 54 opening becomes 27-5/8 by 53-1/2. Enter as fractions or decimals,
the system takes either.

## 5. Reeb doors: slab versus frame, and jamb depth

Door widths in Reeb refer to the **slab**, not the finished unit. A 28, 30, or
34 is the door panel. You still have to account for the frame.

**Jamb depth cannot be changed in the field.** Get it wrong and the door gets
reordered.

- **4-9/16** for a 2x4 wall. This is 70 to 75% of what you will see.
- **6-9/16** for a 2x6 wall.
- **9-1/4** for very thick walls, cinder block and similar. Rare.

## 6. Andersen undersizes doors

Their stated height is the whole product including the frame. Other door
companies quote the panel and add the frame separately.

So **Andersen's 6'8" is actually 79.5 inches.** The doors in the field are
around 82 inches.

**For a standard 6'8" opening you need Andersen's 6'11", which is 82-3/8.**

This catches people. If you select 6'8" because the existing door is a 6'8",
the door will not fit.

## Which Andersen windows match old wood openings

This is not consistent within a series, so do not generalize from one product.

**Match traditional wood window sizes, no customizing needed:**
400 Series Tilt Wash, 400 Series Woodwright

**Do not match, expect to customize:**
400 Series casement, 400 Series awning, 400 Series picture windows, most
casements from any manufacturer

Custom sizing exists in eighth-inch increments. On the double hungs it gets
expensive fast and you probably do not need it. On the 100 Series it is
forgiving and cost-effective.

## One more, on the 100 Series

The frame is **3-1/4 inches per side**, so 6-1/2 inches of any unit dimension
is frame in both directions. A 12 by 12 picture window leaves 5-1/2 inches of
glass. The smaller the unit, the worse it looks. Applies to the gliders, single
hung, casement, and picture windows.

modules.title: Never sell, always include
modules.body_md:
Every rule here has a reason. The reason matters more than the rule, because a
customer will push and you need to be able to explain rather than just refuse.

Most of these exist because we got burned once.

## Never sell

### Locks and hardware

**Therma-Tru multi-point lock.** Not available through us. The distributor
model means panel fit varies, and these break down anywhere from six months to
a few years. Doors that cannot be secured in the field and need repeated
service. Compare with Andersen, who build in-house and make the best
multi-point in the industry.

**Standard plastic locking keeper on the Andersen 100 Series.** Plastic breaks.
Use the metal slimline. See always include below.

### Doors

**Wood-edge economy fiberglass at Reeb.** Reeb's own economy line is a
Therma-Tru with a wood edge. It rots in our humidity. Seen fail in as little as
12 months. Only composite edge: Classic Craft, Fiber Classic, Smooth Star.

**Hardwood adjustable sill.** Hardwood is more durable than the old wood sills
but still breaks down and rots. Composite adjustable never will. Also skip the
value composite adjustable.

**On Guard.** Always standard Frame Saver.

**Raw wood brickmold.** Frame Saver or PVC only. If the door is not
pre-finished, PVC. Never primed pine, clear pine, oak, or mahogany all the way
around the outside. Small price difference, and it will not make or break the
deal.

**Reeb sill pans.** Wildly overpriced. We source locally for far less when we
need one.

### Andersen

**Optional lift hardware on the 400 Series Tilt Wash.** Andersen moved a piece
of framing up for energy performance and the lift hardware no longer lines up.
It sits above the glass. They still sell it. We sold expensive bright brass
hand lifts to a customer who chose the window for them, then could not fit
them. Fine on the Woodwright.

**Sash kits, any brand.** Antiquated and problematic. Most manufacturers have
dropped them. Andersen still offers an E-Series sash replacement kit. We do not
sell it.

**200 Series Tilt Wash.** New construction only. Cannot be used for
replacement.

**Narrowline to Tilt Wash conversion kit.** Hyper specific. Skip it 98 to 99%
of the time.

**Garden and hopper windows.** They appear in the Vendo product list. We do not
sell them.

**Andersen stool.** Expensive and unnecessary. We source locally.

**Andersen arch casing.** We use flex molding, bought locally.

**Andersen exterior trim.** Nice system when it works, but the spacing does not
work in brick openings. We use PVC brickmold. White PVC is close enough to
Andersen white that most people do not paint it.

**Removable interior grilles on any 100 Series window.** Not available.
Simulated divided lite or between the glass only.

**A high-end wood species with paint over it.** Mahogany, cherry, oak, or
maple with a painted finish is money thrown away. Andersen sometimes allows the
combination. If the interior is getting painted, quote pine.

**Third party hardware on an Andersen door.** The multi-point lock is built
into the door and Andersen hardware is what works with it. If a customer
sources their own, we will not install it and we take no responsibility for how
the door operates after that.

**Double bore on an Andersen entry door.** They list it. They do not do it
well, it is problematic, and it is very difficult to modify in the field. A
customer who wants a double bore wants a fiberglass door.

### Glass and vinyl

**Triple pane.** Very expensive, minimal energy gain in the Triangle. Some
competitors push it. If a customer insists you can quote it, but try to talk
them out of it.

**Laminated glass** unless there is a reason. Double strength is strong enough.
Hefty upcharge for no real benefit on an in-home replacement.

**Factory-painted vinyl windows.** We do not offer it. Not a good product.

**Vinyl Design extension jambs.** Raw poplar, unfinished, $50 to $75 per
window, and honestly not well made. Better for our crew to apply them, or for a
contractor to buy their own wood. If a customer pushes, you can quote it.

## Always include, without asking

These are a few dollars each and they prevent headaches. Do not present them as
options.

**Slimline metal hardware on the 100 Series.** Roughly $5 to $10 per window.
Metal instead of plastic.

**Auxiliary foot lock on every Andersen gliding door.** About $30 to $35 on the
400 Series, around $15 on the 100 Series. A real deadbolt shoot bolt, operated
with your foot. Can be drilled for a second position so the door locks while
vented. On a several thousand dollar door it is nothing, and it eliminates the
two-by-four-in-the-track era.

**Sill cover on Reeb doors.** A couple of dollars, protects the sill in
transit.

**Head and sill expanders on Vinyl Design inserts.** If you do not add them
they do not ship. The sill expander in particular is needed to finish the
outside properly.

**Full screen on Andersen windows.** Andersen charges the same for half and
full, so there is no reason to quote a half screen unless the customer asks.
Note that doors are the opposite: they do not default to a screen, and
Andersen's hinged door screen is awkward enough that a phantom screen is the
better answer.

**Unassembled on every Andersen two panel gliding door,** not just the 400
Series. The 100 Series is the only one with no option, and four panel gliders
only come unassembled.

**Knockdown on Andersen gliding doors.** $100 to $200 cheaper, safer to
handle, one person can deliver it, far less damage in transit. Our crews
assemble in 15 to 20 minutes. **The 100 Series is the exception and cannot be
ordered knockdown,** because its frame is integrally built.

**Ask about a key lock on every Andersen door.** It is never a default and it
can run over a hundred dollars. Customers assume it is included, and when
nobody asks, we end up ordering it afterward at our own cost.

quiz.q: A customer specifically wants a multi-point lock on their new Therma-Tru entry door. What do you tell them?
options: Quote it, it is a nice upgrade
We do not sell it. Poor panel fit and it breaks down, sometimes within six months.
Quote it but add a service disclaimer

You are quoting a Reeb door that is not pre-finished. What do you choose for the exterior casing?
options: Clear pine or oak, the customer can stain it

Auxiliary foot lock on Andersen gliding doors

modules.title: Submitting an initial quality request in Andersen Access
modules.body_md:
How we get Andersen to replace or credit something that arrived wrong.

## The steps

Andersen Access, **My Tools**, second item down, **Initial Quality Requests.**

You can review submitted ones from here. **Start New Request.**

Look up the order by Andersen order number, PO number, or quote number. Select
the specific line item with the problem.

## Choosing a resolution

**Service request** if someone has to go out and change a part.
**Replacement** if we need the part sent.
**Credit** if the customer would rather accept the issue and take money back.

Then the expected date with a reason, any special instructions, and a
replacement PO named as customer plus component. "Frager Sash." Your
information autofills.

Save for Later exists if you need to come back.

## Describing the issue

The terms are not self explanatory:

**Aesthetic defect.** A ding, a shift, excessive overfill, a cosmetic problem.

**Damage visible.** The box itself was damaged.

**Concealed damage.** The box was fine and you found the damage on opening.

**Photos are required on everything.** Always.

## Then Pipedrive

Submit, and it appears on the pending requests page. Takes a day or two to
populate.

**Update Pipedrive so we can track the order acknowledgement.**

## Two things that are not software steps

**Check parts before they go to the job site.** The example in the video is an
IQR against an IQR: Andersen sent replacement sashes and one of the
replacements was damaged. It was caught because someone checked before a crew
was standing in a customer's house.

**Filing against a replacement is normal.** Do not assume you have made a
mistake.

quiz.q: A box arrived intact and you found a damaged sash inside. Which issue type?
What is always required on an initial quality request?
What do you do after submitting?
options: Update Pipedrive so we can track the order acknowledgement
Wait for the replacement to arrive

modules.title: Quoting big doors and Andersen entry doors in Vendo
modules.body_md:
Advanced tier. Two things we do not sell often, covered together.

Andersen calls the moving glass wall systems **big doors**, which is a fairly
silly marketing name, but it is what they went with. Bifold and multi-glide.

## The three numbers to know before anything else

**$1,700 to $2,300 per linear foot,** depending on how it is built and
configured.

That is **the door only.** No labor, no wall work, no engineering.

A 16 foot opening is tens of thousands of dollars before anyone picks up a
tool.

People see these on HGTV and design shows and have no idea what they cost.
Knowing the range means you can find out in thirty seconds whether this is a
real conversation.

## Why you cannot quote it at the table

**No stock sizes.** Everything is custom.

**Minimum 2x6 wall, often more.** If it is not a new construction opening being
built for it, the wall will probably have to be modified, and that means
engineer reports.

**There are no adders in Vendo for these.** Look and you will not find them. No
standard installation price exists, because it depends entirely on the size and
the project. Labor is a custom quote.

You can build the door in Vendo and give a rough idea of the door cost. You
cannot give a price on the spot.

**Realistic timeline: one to two weeks minimum.** An engineer likely has to
come out, the project manager or the installing crew has to see it, and we have
to confirm the build and availability with Andersen. This is nothing like the
24 to 48 hours on a Reeb special order.

## The sales advice that matters most

If you are quoting a whole house and they also want a big door, **quote the
rest of the house and break the big door out into a second appointment or a
second package.**

Close the deal on everything else. Do not let a one to two week engineering
process hold up a house full of windows.

## The economical alternative

Before you deep dive a big door, find out what they actually want.

If they are after that wide open feel, **the 200 Series, 400 Series, or
E-Series four panel gliding doors** get you a very similar look. They customize
up to roughly 16 feet and they are significantly less expensive.

**We never use the word cheap.** More economical, less expensive, better value.
Not cheap.

## The pass-through window, and Andersen does not tell you this

If a customer mentions Andersen's **pass-through window**, that is a multi-glide
door or a folding patio door. They are the same product. Andersen just markets
it under a different name and never says so.

You quote it under multi-glide patio door. Because these are fully custom, they
can be made small. A kitchen opening onto a patio for passing food out is a
real use case.

## Building a multi-glide

Traditional or contemporary profile. Most people buying these want light, so
contemporary is the likely pick.

Measurement type is frame size or rough opening. No stock sizes.

Configuration codes read from the exterior. **S3L** is one stationary panel and
three sliding left. There are a lot of combinations.

Glass, grilles, hardware, and locks work like every other Andersen quote.

**Sills, and one of these is a hard rule:**

- **On-floor drainage** is the traditional sill and **the most energy efficient
  and airtight.**
- **Flush** is recessed into the floor for a completely smooth transition.
- **On-floor low threshold** sits between them, less of a trip hazard.

**The flush sill requires a concrete floor.** It cannot go into a wood floor.
Andersen's own installation instructions still show wood, but from an
engineering standpoint, after how they have revised it over the last few years,
concrete only. If there is no concrete, it is a traditional sill.

Frame configuration is jamb to jamb, meaning it closes against the wall, or
pocket, where the panels disappear into the wall. That is separate from which
direction they travel.

Panel stack location is whether the stacked panels end up inside or outside.

Power operator automation is available if they want the door motorized.

## Building a bifold

Same flow. Copy your previous choices to move faster.

Configuration codes work the same way. **5L** is five panels folding left. You
can set one panel to swing independently as the everyday door, so they are not
opening the whole wall to walk outside.

**Minimum 6-9/16 wall depth** on bifolds.

Same sill logic, same concrete rule on flush.

## Andersen entry doors

Different product entirely, and we rarely sell them. Maybe eight to ten in
fifteen years.

Two reasons. They have always been expensive, although compared with what
fiberglass costs now that is less true. And **the options are extremely
limited.** Half light, six panel, a craftsman style, and that is about it.

**Do not bring them up.** You will sell a fiberglass door almost every time.
Only quote one if a customer is specifically asking for it.

If you do:

**Their residential entry doors use traditional door sizes,** unlike their
patio doors. So a 3'0" by 6'8" is genuinely a 6'8". Ironic, and worth knowing
so you do not apply the undersizing rule here.

Wood inside and out, or aluminum clad.

**Panel thickness: 1-3/4 as standard.** They also offer 2-1/4. Default to
1-3/4 unless someone asks.

**Multi-point lock, always.** They offer a single point but there is no reason
to take it. Andersen's multi-point is a solid product.

**Never sell a double bore Andersen door.** They list it, but they do not do it
well, it is problematic, and it is very hard to modify in the field. If a
customer wants a double bore, that is a fiberglass door.

**Unlike big doors, entry doors do have adders.** Single door installation.
Capture it.
